    # 15 — Dependency-ordered implementation tickets
    
    Use one small PR per ticket unless two changes are tightly inseparable. `INT` = `integration` Azahar branch, `EXP` = `experimental` branch, `RUST` = product repo. Every PR links its regression test and source SHA. **No code below has been implemented as part of this dossier.**
    
    ## Wave 0 — pin sources and reduce integration risk
    
    ### T00 [RUST] Repository skeleton and toolchain lock
    
    **Deliver:** Cargo workspace, empty crates, `rust-toolchain.toml`, source-version manifest, CI format/check. **Check:** `cargo test --workspace` passes; no network downloads at runtime. **Avoid:** implementing service APIs before machine boundary is known.
    
    ### T01 [INT] Fork/worktree policy and stock baseline
    
    **Deliver:** `integration` branch from selected upstream SHA, `experimental` from integration, immutable stock checkout; patch inventory; build matrix. **Check:** stock Azahar builds and launches homebrew fixture; revisions recorded. **Avoid:** moving branches as build inputs without pinned hashes.
    
    ### T02 [RUST] GPUI screen spike, no emulator
    
    **Deliver:** standalone GPUI app with generated native-resolution top/bottom images, scaling, touch coordinate tests, memory/perf observation. **Check:** 10-minute continuous updates, 4 simulated sessions, two high-DPI scale factors. **Avoid:** native Vulkan interop in this ticket.
    
    ### T03 [RUST] Protocol scaffold and supervisor stubs
    
    **Deliver:** envelope schema, handshake, typed status codes, local pipe/socket transport, mock worker, process lifecycle state machine and unit tests. **Check:** invalid messages rejected; worker crash detected; stale epoch rejected; GUI-independent CLI can query mock. **Avoid:** encoding C++ pointer values into protocol.
    
    ## Wave 1 — native Azahar worker
    
    ### T04 [INT] New CMake worker target
    
    **Files:** root `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`, new `src/ctr_worker`. **Deliver:** `ENABLE_CTR_WORKER=OFF` default; executable linked to native libs. **Check:** Qt-off/Libretro-off build; stock build behavior unchanged. **Avoid:** modifying `citra_libretro`.
    
    ### T05 [INT] Minimal headless frontend
    
    **Files:** `emu_window.h` adapter, worker main, required applet/image callbacks. **Deliver:** boot known `.3dsx`; emit lifecycle and error result. **Check:** no Qt/SDL windows, clean stop/restart; unsupported applets explicit. **Avoid:** assuming `Headless` provides screenshot capture.
    
    ### T06 [INT] Native frame output
    
    **Deliver:** software backend raw top/bottom buffers with format/orientation metadata and sequence/ring ownership. **Check:** compare stable images to stock Azahar, test stale leases and source layout; no use-after-free. **Avoid:** scaling images for capture or blocking core waiting on UI.
    
    ### T07 [INT] Input/audio adapters
    
    **Deliver:** buttons, touch, scripted-exclusive input channel; bounded audio ring, optional muted output; keyboard/applicant fallback events. **Check:** timed key/touch replay, output hashes, headless audio drain, device disconnect. **Avoid:** mixing live input into deterministic script.
    
    ### T08 [INT+RUST] Safe-point command queue + IPC integration
    
    **Files:** `core.cpp` pending work, worker queue, Rust transport client. **Deliver:** load/run/pause/reset/status/stop; bounded read-only register/memory inspection, notification waking. **Check:** concurrent read/control requests while frame limiter sleeps; no mutable-state cross-thread access. **Avoid:** claiming selected-core instruction steps until proven.
    
    ### T09 [INT+RUST] Per-instance roots and shutdown
    
    **Deliver:** private settings/save/cache/log paths, unique IPC endpoints, worker termination and recovery. **Check:** two workers simultaneously read same ROM but write separate saves; forced-kill of one does not damage other. **Avoid:** incomplete COW layered filesystem at this stage.
    
    ## Wave 2 — first useful new emulator
    
    ### T10 [RUST] GPUI worker display and session browser
    
    **Deliver:** streamed images, input routing, run control, lifecycle warnings, session switching/docking. **Check:** worker crash does not crash UI; touch mapping correct at zoom/HiDPI; only latest displayed frames consumed. **Avoid:** full-featured GPU panes before stable state snapshots.
    
    ### T11 [RUST] Headless CLI and fixture runner
    
    **Deliver:** `create/load/run_until/capture/stop`, scenario format, checkpoints, input lease, report manifest. **Check:** fixed homebrew demo has repeatable result across 3 runs and no unbounded scenario execution. **Avoid:** falsely labeling host timing as hardware time.
    
    ### T12 [RUST] Four-worker stress and failure injection
    
    **Deliver:** resource policy and unique artifact roots. **Check:** 4 workers run independent scenarios, one forced crash, no port/cache/saves collision. **Avoid:** unbounded trace memory per worker.
    
    ### T13 [RUST] MCP adapter
    
    **Deliver:** small typed tools for session/control/capture/queries, artifact resources, client permissions. **Check:** CLI/MCP parity and no access to arbitrary shell/filesystem. **Avoid:** direct MCP calls into Azahar UDP RPC.
    
    ## Wave 3 — targeted engineering debugger
    
    ### T14 [EXP] CPU/kernel/thread trace
    
    **Deliver:** pause reasons, SVC/IPC and thread events, register/disassembly snapshots, breakpoint tests. **Check:** deterministic crash fixture yields same stop reason/context; perf A/B. **Avoid:** global instruction-by-instruction logging.
    
    ### T15 [EXP] GPU event indices and command capture
    
    **Files:** `gpu.cpp`, `pica_core.cpp`; **deliver:** GSP command IDs, PICA command stream, per-draw identity with state/time. **Check:** draw IDs stable for selected test, capture matches actual pre-draw command, bounded loss accounting. **Avoid:** capture of live VRAM long after draw.
    
    ### T16 [EXP] Resource lineage and GPU image capture
    
    **Deliver:** texture/surface source versions, transfer events, native pixel/diff images, renderer sync. **Check:** CPU overwrite between two draws distinguishes resource versions, no false identical hashes. **Avoid:** equating host texture format with original 3DS bytes.
    
    ### T17 [RUST] Timeline and visual inspector panels
    
    **Deliver:** CPU/kernel/GPU lanes, draw-state diffs, texture/shader tables, snapshot selector, stable source labels. **Check:** 100k-event trace opens without blocking GPUI event loop; resource usage bounded. **Avoid:** expensive polling for hidden panels.
    
    ### T18 [RUST+EXP] Differential run analysis
    
    **Deliver:** aligned checkpoint, frame and draw structural diffs; report earliest reliable divergence; corpus runner across stock/integration/experimental. **Check:** synthetic deliberate divergence detected; no nondeterminism misdiagnosed as definite bug. **Avoid:** reliance solely on screenshot visual comparison.
    
    ## Wave 4 — accuracy research
    
    ### T19 [RUST/hardware] Coffeepot 3DS microbenchmark integration
    
    **Deliver:** physical-console harness/suite, metadata parser, timer overhead calibration, raw fixture corpus. **Check:** first 3 physical experiments reproduced in separate sessions and compared to Azahar. **Avoid:** crediting unrun code as hardware-verified.
    
    ### T20 [EXP] Expose timing assumptions
    
    **Deliver:** list of virtual tick/transfer completion assumptions, tracing of source parameters and output event times, configured deterministic ticks. **Check:** trace accounts for timing events with correct domains; regression suite unaffected when disabled. **Avoid:** replacing model with game-specific per-title waits.
    
    ### T21 [RUST/EXP] Independent PICA register/shader reference
    
    **Deliver:** Rust component able to parse selected command lists and execute a minimal shader/reference draw; differential fixtures. **Check:** known hardware outputs match, with errors cataloged; feature-gated and doesn't break integrated backend. **Avoid:** promising full PICA rasterizer on first PR.
    
    ### T22 [EXP] First measured GPU timing correction
    
    **Deliver:** one documented timing behavior modeled against isolated and held-out physical tests. **Check:** improved physical error on target cases without known regressions, release flag and confidence labels. **Avoid:** accuracy claims from host profiler measurements.
    
    ### T23 [RUST] CPU and memory reference emulator research track
    
    **Deliver:** small ARM11 interpreter/test harness, architectural conformance tests and cache/timing experiment plan. **Check:** instruction results match hardware cases; no requirement to boot games yet. **Avoid:** replacing working Dynarmic prematurely.
    
    ## Architectural decisions still to research
    
    - Exact worker ownership of separate renderer/audio threads; benchmark best race-free safe-point boundary.
    - Whether real renderer exports native screen buffers conveniently without render-to-surface changes.
    - Whether a shared immutable shader cache is safe across worker processes.
    - GPUI texture import API viability; postpone until native-frame pipeline has measured limitations.
    - Complete save-state fidelity across worker revisions; scripted checkpoint remains fallback.
    - Independent native firmware boot path and distribution constraints.
    
    ## PR review form
    
    For each ticket include: `source SHA`, `branch`, `touched native files`, `why implementation belongs here`, `feature flag`, `before/after command or screenshot artifact`, `tests performed`, `hardware verification status`, `host performance A/B`, `known risk`, `rollback`. See templates.
    //! Bounded local control messages. Large images never travel on this channel.
    use std::io::{self, Read, Write};
    
    use serde::de::DeserializeOwned;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    
    /// Maximum encoded control message, checked before allocation.
    pub const MAX_CONTROL_BYTES: u32 = 65_536;
    
    /// Commands implemented by the supervisor spike.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum Method {
        Hello,
        Status,
        Stop,
    }
    
    /// Completion status; OK always means completed, never merely queued.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum Status {
        Ok,
        InvalidArgument,
        Unsupported,
        NotReady,
        StaleEpoch,
        PermissionDenied,
    }
    
    /// Request envelope for one inherited private pipe connection.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    pub struct Request {
        pub version_major: u16,
        pub version_minor: u16,
        pub request_id: u64,
        pub session: String,
        pub epoch: u64,
        pub method: Method,
    }
    
    /// Response envelope. Mock identity is explicit and has no emulator capabilities.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    pub struct Reply {
        pub version_major: u16,
        pub version_minor: u16,
        pub request_id: u64,
        pub session: String,
        pub epoch: u64,
        pub status: Status,
        pub state: String,
        pub backend: String,
    }
    
    /// Encode a JSON control message behind a little-endian u32 byte count.
    pub fn encode<T: Serialize>(value: &T) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let payload = serde_json::to_vec(value).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
        let length = u32::try_from(payload.len()).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
        validate_length(length)?;
        let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(payload.len() + 4);
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&length.to_le_bytes());
        bytes.extend_from_slice(&payload);
        Ok(bytes)
    }
    
    /// Reject invalid lengths before allocating payload storage.
    pub fn validate_length(length: u32) -> io::Result<()> {
        if length == 0 || length > MAX_CONTROL_BYTES {
            return Err(io::Error::new(
                io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                "invalid control length",
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Read exactly one bounded message; truncation is an error.
    pub fn read<T: DeserializeOwned>(reader: &mut impl Read) -> io::Result<T> {
        let mut prefix = [0; 4];
        reader.read_exact(&mut prefix)?;
        let length = u32::from_le_bytes(prefix);
        validate_length(length)?;
        let mut payload = vec![0; length as usize];
        reader.read_exact(&mut payload)?;
        serde_json::from_slice(&payload).map_err(io::Error::other)
    }
    
    /// Write and flush a complete message.
    pub fn write<T: Serialize>(writer: &mut impl Write, value: &T) -> io::Result<()> {
        writer.write_all(&encode(value)?)?;
        writer.flush()
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        #[test]
        fn invalid_lengths_and_truncated_json_are_rejected() {
            for length in [0, MAX_CONTROL_BYTES + 1, u32::MAX] {
                assert!(read::<Request>(&mut length.to_le_bytes().as_slice()).is_err());
            }
            assert!(read::<Request>(&mut [2, 0, 0, 0, b'{'].as_slice()).is_err());
            assert!(read::<Request>(&mut [2, 0, 0, 0, b'{', b'}'].as_slice()).is_err());
        }
    }
    //! Supervisor for a single inherited private pipe connection.
    //!
    //! All exchanges are serialized by mutable ownership. A failed or timed-out
    //! exchange destroys the connection: a possibly committed request is never retried.
    use std::fs::{self, File};
    use std::io;
    
    use std::process::Stdio;
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_protocol::control::{self, Method, Reply, Request, Status};
    use lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid;
    use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
    use tokio::process::{Child, ChildStdin, ChildStdout, Command};
    
    use crate::{SessionState, WorkerSpec};
    
    /// Owns the child and its unshared pipe ends. Drop kills the direct child.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct ControlledWorker {
        child: Child,
        input: ChildStdin,
        output: ChildStdout,
        session: String,
        next_request: u64,
        epoch: u64,
        state: SessionState,
        timeout: Duration,
    }
    
    impl ControlledWorker {
        /// Launch, retain stderr locally, and complete a bounded handshake.
        pub async fn spawn(spec: &WorkerSpec, timeout: Duration) -> io::Result<Self> {
            if timeout.is_zero() || timeout > Duration::from_secs(30) {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
                    "timeout must be in (0, 30s]",
                ));
            }
            fs::create_dir_all(&spec.storage_root)?;
            let stderr = File::create(spec.storage_root.join("worker.stderr.log"))?;
            let mut command = Command::new(&spec.executable);
            command
                .args(&spec.args)
                .envs(spec.env.iter().cloned())
                .env("LOTUS_STORAGE_ROOT", &spec.storage_root)
                .stdin(Stdio::piped())
                .stdout(Stdio::piped())
                .stderr(stderr)
                .kill_on_drop(true);
            #[cfg(windows)]
            command.creation_flags(0x0800_0000);
            let mut child = command.spawn()?;
            let input = child
                .stdin
                .take()
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("missing child stdin"))?;
            let output = child
                .stdout
                .take()
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("missing child stdout"))?;
            let mut worker = Self {
                child,
                input,
                output,
                session: SessionUuid::generate().to_string(),
                next_request: 1,
                epoch: 1,
                state: SessionState::Created,
                timeout,
            };
            worker.request(Method::Hello).await?;
            worker.state = SessionState::Idle;
            Ok(worker)
        }
    
        /// Current supervisor state; poll status to detect a newly exited process.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn state(&self) -> SessionState {
            self.state
        }
    
        /// Child OS identifier, absent after reaping.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn pid(&self) -> Option<u32> {
            self.child.id()
        }
    
        /// Query the worker without any GUI dependencies.
        pub async fn status(&mut self) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            self.request(Method::Status).await
        }
    
        /// Complete shutdown and reap; kill on any failed exchange or exit deadline.
        pub async fn stop(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> {
            self.request(Method::Stop).await?;
            match tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, self.child.wait()).await {
                Ok(Ok(status)) if status.success() => {
                    self.state = SessionState::Stopped;
                    Ok(())
                }
                _ => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    Err(io::Error::other("worker failed to exit cleanly"))
                }
            }
        }
    
        async fn fail(&mut self) {
            self.state = SessionState::Crashed;
            let _ = self.child.kill().await;
            let _ = self.child.wait().await;
        }
    
        async fn request(&mut self, method: Method) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            if matches!(self.state, SessionState::Stopped | SessionState::Crashed) {
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe,
                    "worker is no longer active",
                ));
            }
            let request = Request {
                version_major: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAJOR,
                version_minor: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MINOR,
                request_id: self.next_request,
                session: self.session.clone(),
                epoch: self.epoch,
                method,
            };
            self.next_request = self
                .next_request
                .checked_add(1)
                .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::other("request ID exhausted"))?;
            let result = tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, self.exchange(&request)).await;
            let reply = match result {
                Ok(Ok(reply)) => reply,
                Ok(Err(error)) => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    return Err(error);
                }
                Err(_) => {
                    self.fail().await;
                    return Err(io::Error::new(
                        io::ErrorKind::TimedOut,
                        "worker exchange deadline exceeded; result unknown",
                    ));
                }
            };
            if !lotus_protocol::is_compatible(reply.version_major, reply.version_minor)
                || reply.request_id != request.request_id
                || reply.session != self.session
                || reply.epoch != self.epoch
                || reply.status != Status::Ok
                || (method == Method::Stop && reply.state != "stopped")
                || (method != Method::Stop && reply.state != "idle")
            {
                self.fail().await;
                return Err(io::Error::new(
                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,
                    "invalid worker reply identity, epoch, status or state",
                ));
            }
            Ok(reply)
        }
    
        async fn exchange(&mut self, request: &Request) -> io::Result<Reply> {
            self.input.write_all(&control::encode(request)?).await?;
            self.input.flush().await?;
            let length = self.output.read_u32_le().await?;
            control::validate_length(length)?;
            let mut payload = vec![0; length as usize];
            self.output.read_exact(&mut payload).await?;
            serde_json::from_slice(&payload).map_err(io::Error::other)
        }
    }
    //! `ctr-cli`: headless access to the Lotus tooling.
    //!
    //! The CLI shares the same typed operations as the desktop application and
    //! the MCP server. It never opens a window and never requires a GUI session.
    
    use anyhow::{bail, Context, Result};
    use lotus_protocol::protocol_id;
    use lotus_runner::Scenario;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    
    /// Pinned revisions, mirrored from `config/pins.toml`.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    struct Pins {
        azahar: AzaharPins,
        gpui: GpuiPins,
        rust: RustPins,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    struct AzaharPins {
        repository: String,
        fork: String,
        upstream_commit: String,
        integration_branch: String,
        integration_commit: String,
        experimental_branch: String,
        experimental_commit: String,
        vendor_path: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    struct GpuiPins {
        repository: String,
        rev: String,
        crate_version: String,
    }
    
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    struct RustPins {
        channel: String,
        host: String,
    }
    
    /// Usage text.
    const USAGE: &str = "\
    ctr-cli: Lotus command line interface
    
    Usage:
      ctr-cli version              Print the Lotus version and worker protocol version
      ctr-cli mock <worker-executable> Query a mock worker over private pipes
      ctr-cli pins                 Print the pinned Azahar and GPUI revisions
      ctr-cli scenario validate <path>
                                    Validate a scenario file against the execution limits
    ";
    
    fn main() -> Result<()> {
        let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
        let command = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("help");
    
        match command {
            "version" => {
                println!("lotus {}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
                println!("worker protocol {}", protocol_id());
            }
            "pins" => {
                let pins = load_pins()?;
                println!("{}", toml::to_string_pretty(&pins)?);
            }
            "mock" => {
                let executable = args
                    .get(1)
                    .context("usage: ctr-cli mock <worker-executable>")?;
                let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
                    "lotus-cli-{}",
                    lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid::generate()
                ));
                let spec = lotus_session::WorkerSpec::new(executable, &root);
                let runtime = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
                runtime.block_on(async {
                    let mut worker = lotus_session::controlled_worker::ControlledWorker::spawn(
                        &spec,
                        std::time::Duration::from_secs(3),
                    )
                    .await?;
                    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&worker.status().await?)?);
                    worker.stop().await
                })?;
            }
            "scenario" => {
                let sub = args.get(1).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("help");
                match sub {
                    "validate" => {
                        let path = args
                            .get(2)
                            .context("usage: ctr-cli scenario validate <path>")?;
                        let scenario = Scenario::load(path)
                            .with_context(|| format!("cannot load scenario {path}"))?;
                        scenario
                            .validate()
                            .with_context(|| format!("scenario {path} is invalid"))?;
                        println!("scenario {} is valid", scenario.name);
                    }
                    _ => {
                        println!("{USAGE}");
                        bail!("unknown scenario subcommand: {sub}");
                    }
                }
            }
            "help" | "--help" | "-h" => println!("{USAGE}"),
            other => {
                println!("{USAGE}");
                bail!("unknown command: {other}");
            }
        }
    
        Ok(())
    }
    
    /// Load the pinned revision manifest.
    fn load_pins() -> Result<Pins> {
        let path = pins_path();
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .with_context(|| format!("cannot read {}", path.display()))?;
        toml::from_str(&text).with_context(|| format!("cannot parse {}", path.display()))
    }
    
    /// Location of the pinned revision manifest.
    fn pins_path() -> PathBuf {
        // The manifest lives in the repository root. Walk up from the crate
        // directory so the CLI works from a source checkout and from a build
        // directory inside the repository.
        let manifest = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"));
        let mut root = manifest.as_path();
        while let Some(parent) = root.parent() {
            if parent.join("config").join("pins.toml").is_file() {
                return parent.join("config").join("pins.toml");
            }
            root = parent;
        }
        manifest.join("../../config/pins.toml")
    }
    //! Model Context Protocol server for the Lotus session supervisor.
    //!
    //! The MCP server is an adapter, not a second debugger. Every tool it
    //! exposes goes through the same typed session operations that the desktop
    //! application and the CLI use. It is local only: there is no remote listener
    //! and no unauthenticated RPC endpoint.
    
    use lotus_runner::Scenario;
    use lotus_session::SessionManager;
    use lotus_trace::EventCategory;
    use rmcp::handler::server::router::tool::ToolRouter;
    use rmcp::handler::server::wrapper::Parameters;
    use rmcp::model::{CallToolResult, ContentBlock, ServerCapabilities, ServerConfig};
    use rmcp::{tool, tool_handler, tool_router, ErrorData, ServerHandler};
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
    
    /// Arguments of the scenario validation tool.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    pub struct ValidateScenarioArgs {
        /// Path of the scenario file, relative to the working directory of the
        /// server or absolute.
        pub path: String,
    }
    
    /// The MCP server.
    #[derive(Clone)]
    pub struct LotusServer {
        tool_router: ToolRouter<Self>,
        sessions: Arc<Mutex<SessionManager>>,
        storage_root: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl LotusServer {
        /// Create a server with an empty session registry.
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self::with_storage_root(default_storage_root())
        }
    
        /// Create a server that keeps session storage below `storage_root`.
        pub fn with_storage_root(storage_root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            Self {
                tool_router: Self::tool_router(),
                sessions: Arc::new(Mutex::new(SessionManager::new())),
                storage_root: storage_root.into(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Storage root used by this server.
        pub fn storage_root(&self) -> &std::path::Path {
            &self.storage_root
        }
    
        /// Number of sessions currently known to the supervisor.
        pub fn session_count(&self) -> usize {
            self.sessions
                .lock()
                .map(|manager| manager.len())
                .unwrap_or(0)
        }
    }
    
    impl Default for LotusServer {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self::new()
        }
    }
    
    #[tool_router(router = tool_router)]
    impl LotusServer {
        /// Report the state of the Lotus server.
        #[tool(
            description = "Report the Lotus server status: worker protocol version, session count and event categories."
        )]
        pub async fn lotus_status(&self) -> String {
            let status = serde_json::json!({
                "protocol_version": lotus_protocol::protocol_id(),
                "sessions": self.session_count(),
                "storage_root": self.storage_root.display().to_string(),
                "event_categories": event_category_ids(),
            });
            status.to_string()
        }
    
        /// List the sessions known to the supervisor.
        #[tool(description = "List the emulator sessions currently known to the Lotus supervisor.")]
        pub async fn lotus_list_sessions(&self) -> String {
            let ids = match self.sessions.lock() {
                Ok(manager) => manager
                    .ids()
                    .iter()
                    .map(|id| id.to_string())
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                Err(_) => Vec::new(),
            };
            serde_json::json!({ "sessions": ids }).to_string()
        }
    
        /// Validate a scenario file.
        #[tool(
            description = "Load a scenario file and report whether it satisfies the project's execution limits."
        )]
        pub async fn lotus_validate_scenario(
            &self,
            Parameters(args): Parameters<ValidateScenarioArgs>,
        ) -> Result<CallToolResult, ErrorData> {
            let path = PathBuf::from(&args.path);
            match Scenario::load(&path) {
                Ok(scenario) => match scenario.validate() {
                    Ok(()) => Ok(CallToolResult::success(vec![ContentBlock::text(
                        serde_json::json!({
                            "path": args.path,
                            "valid": true,
                            "name": scenario.name,
                            "max_frames": scenario.stop.max_frames,
                        })
                        .to_string(),
                    )])),
                    Err(error) => Ok(CallToolResult::error(vec![ContentBlock::text(format!(
                        "scenario is invalid: {error}"
                    ))])),
                },
                Err(error) => Ok(CallToolResult::error(vec![ContentBlock::text(format!(
                    "cannot load scenario: {error}"
                ))])),
            }
        }
    
        /// List the event categories the trace layer records.
        #[tool(description = "List the structured event categories the Lotus trace layer can record.")]
        pub async fn lotus_event_categories(&self) -> String {
            serde_json::json!({ "categories": event_category_ids() }).to_string()
        }
    }
    
    #[tool_handler(router = self.tool_router)]
    impl ServerHandler for LotusServer {
        fn get_info(&self) -> ServerConfig {
            ServerConfig::new(ServerCapabilities::builder().enable_tools().build()).with_instructions(
                "Lotus exposes the emulator session supervisor to agents. Tools are local only and \
                 operate on sessions created by the host application. Raw traces and captures are \
                 returned as artifact references, never as inline payloads.",
            )
        }
    }
    
    /// Identifiers of every known event category.
    fn event_category_ids() -> Vec<&'static str> {
        vec![
            EventCategory::Worker.id(),
            EventCategory::GpuSubmitCmdList.id(),
            EventCategory::GpuDraw.id(),
            EventCategory::Cpu.id(),
            EventCategory::Memory.id(),
            EventCategory::ServiceCall.id(),
            EventCategory::KernelIpc.id(),
            EventCategory::Exception.id(),
        ]
    }
    
    /// Default location of the per-session storage roots.
    fn default_storage_root() -> PathBuf {
        std::env::temp_dir().join("lotus-sessions")
    }

    /**
     * This class is an interface for an audio sink. An audio sink accepts samples in stereo signed
     * PCM16 format to be output. Sinks *do not* handle resampling and expect the correct sample rate.
     * They are dumb outputs.
     */
    class Sink {
    public:
        virtual ~Sink() = default;
    
        /// The native rate of this sink. The sink expects to be fed samples that respect this.
        /// (Units: samples/sec)
        virtual unsigned int GetNativeSampleRate() const = 0;
    
        /**
         * Set callback for samples
         * @param samples Samples in interleaved stereo PCM16 format.
         * @param sample_count Number of samples.
         */
        virtual void SetCallback(std::function<void(s16*, std::size_t)> cb) = 0;
    
        /**
         * Override and set this to true if the sink wants audio data submitted
         * immediately rather than requesting audio on demand
         * @return true if audio data should be pushed to the sink
         */
        virtual bool ImmediateSubmission() {
            return false;
        }
    
        /**
         * Push audio samples directly to the sink, bypassing the FIFO.
         * Only called when ImmediateSubmission() returns true.
         * @param data Pointer to stereo PCM16 samples (each sample is L+R pair)
         * @param num_samples Number of stereo samples
         */
        virtual void PushSamples(const void* data, std::size_t num_samples) {}
    };
    
    } // namespace AudioCore
    //! Scenario definition and validation.
    //!
    //! A scenario is a reproducible, bounded run: fixed content, fixed input
    //! schedule, a stop condition and explicit assertions. Every scenario is
    //! validated before it runs, because an unbounded scenario can exhaust the
    //! host or hang a test suite.
    
    use lotus_session::worker::WorkerFlavor;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::path::Path;
    use thiserror::Error;
    
    /// Maximum frames a scenario may request.
    pub const MAX_SCENARIO_FRAMES: u64 = 100_000;
    /// Maximum wall clock time a scenario may request, in seconds.
    pub const MAX_SCENARIO_WALL_SECONDS: u64 = 3_600;
    /// Maximum bytes a single capture may request.
    pub const MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES: u64 = 512 * 1024 * 1024;
    
    /// Errors raised while loading or validating a scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Error)]
    pub enum ScenarioError {
        /// The file could not be read.
        #[error("cannot read scenario {path}: {source}")]
        Io {
            /// Scenario path.
            path: String,
            /// Underlying error.
            #[source]
            source: std::io::Error,
        },
        /// The file is not valid YAML for this schema.
        #[error("cannot parse scenario: {0}")]
        Parse(#[source] serde_yaml::Error),
        /// The scenario is not valid.
        #[error("invalid scenario: {0}")]
        Invalid(String),
    }
    
    /// Content loaded by a scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Content {
        /// Content kind, e.g. `homebrew_3dsx`.
        pub kind: String,
        /// Path of the content relative to the scenario file.
        pub path_handle: String,
        /// Expected SHA-256 of the content, if known.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub sha256: Option<String>,
    }
    
    /// Emulation profile of a scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Profile {
        /// Console model.
        pub model: String,
        /// Render backend.
        pub renderer: String,
        /// Azahar branch flavour.
        pub worker_flavor: WorkerFlavor,
        /// Initial deterministic tick value.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub deterministic_initial_ticks: Option<u64>,
        /// Audio output mode; `discard` still runs the DSP.
        #[serde(default = "default_audio_output")]
        pub audio_output: String,
    }
    
    fn default_audio_output() -> String {
        "discard".to_string()
    }
    
    /// Storage isolation of a scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Storage {
        /// Storage mode, e.g. `isolated_copy`.
        pub mode: String,
        /// Base snapshot the run starts from.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub base_snapshot: Option<String>,
    }
    
    /// Input schedule entry.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct InputEvent {
        /// Frame the event is injected at.
        pub at_frame: u64,
        /// Button name.
        pub button: String,
        /// `down`, `up` or `press`.
        pub action: String,
    }
    
    /// Input ownership and schedule.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Input {
        /// Owner of input during the run; `scenario` disables live input.
        pub owner: String,
        /// Scheduled events.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub schedule: Vec<InputEvent>,
    }
    
    /// Stop condition of a scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Stop {
        /// Maximum number of frames.
        pub max_frames: u64,
        /// Wall clock limit in seconds.
        pub wall_timeout_seconds: u64,
    }
    
    /// When a capture is taken.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct CaptureWhen {
        /// Frame the capture is taken at.
        pub frame: Option<u64>,
        /// Event name that triggers the capture.
        pub event: Option<String>,
    }
    
    /// A single capture request.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Capture {
        /// Trigger.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub when: Option<CaptureWhen>,
        /// What to include.
        pub include: Vec<String>,
        /// Maximum size of the capture.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub max_bytes: Option<u64>,
    }
    
    /// A scenario assertion.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Assertion {
        /// Assertion type, e.g. `event_seen`.
        #[serde(rename = "type")]
        pub kind: String,
        /// Event name for `event_seen`.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub event: Option<String>,
        /// Minimum count for `event_seen`.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub count_at_least: Option<u64>,
        /// Minimum frame count for `frame_count`.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub minimum: Option<u64>,
    }
    
    /// Output retention policy.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Outputs {
        /// Artifacts that are retained.
        pub retain: Vec<String>,
    }
    
    /// A complete scenario.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct Scenario {
        /// Scenario schema version.
        pub version: u32,
        /// Scenario name.
        pub name: String,
        /// Content to load.
        pub content: Content,
        /// Emulation profile.
        pub profile: Profile,
        /// Storage isolation.
        pub storage: Storage,
        /// Input schedule.
        pub input: Input,
        /// Stop condition.
        pub stop: Stop,
        /// Captures.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub captures: Vec<Capture>,
        /// Assertions.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub assertions: Vec<Assertion>,
        /// Output retention.
        #[serde(default)]
        pub outputs: Outputs,
    }
    
    impl Scenario {
        /// Load a scenario from a YAML file.
        pub fn load(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, ScenarioError> {
            let path = path.as_ref();
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|source| ScenarioError::Io {
                path: path.display().to_string(),
                source,
            })?;
            let scenario: Scenario = serde_yaml::from_str(&text).map_err(ScenarioError::Parse)?;
            Ok(scenario)
        }
    
        /// Validate the scenario against the project's execution limits.
        pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), ScenarioError> {
            if self.version != 1 {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                    "unsupported scenario version {}",
                    self.version
                )));
            }
            if self.name.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid("scenario name is empty".to_string()));
            }
            if self.stop.max_frames == 0 {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(
                    "stop.max_frames must be greater than zero".to_string(),
                ));
            }
            if self.stop.max_frames > MAX_SCENARIO_FRAMES {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                    "stop.max_frames {} exceeds the limit of {MAX_SCENARIO_FRAMES}",
                    self.stop.max_frames
                )));
            }
            if self.stop.wall_timeout_seconds == 0 {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(
                    "stop.wall_timeout_seconds must be greater than zero".to_string(),
                ));
            }
            if self.stop.wall_timeout_seconds > MAX_SCENARIO_WALL_SECONDS {
                return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                    "stop.wall_timeout_seconds {} exceeds the limit of {MAX_SCENARIO_WALL_SECONDS}",
                    self.stop.wall_timeout_seconds
                )));
            }
    
            let mut previous_frame = 0u64;
            for event in &self.input.schedule {
                if event.at_frame > self.stop.max_frames {
                    return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                        "input event at frame {} is beyond stop.max_frames {}",
                        event.at_frame, self.stop.max_frames
                    )));
                }
                if event.at_frame < previous_frame {
                    return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(
                        "input schedule is not ordered by frame".to_string(),
                    ));
                }
                previous_frame = event.at_frame;
            }
    
            for capture in &self.captures {
                if let Some(max_bytes) = capture.max_bytes {
                    if max_bytes > MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES {
                        return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                            "capture max_bytes {max_bytes} exceeds the limit of {MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES}"
                        )));
                    }
                }
            }
    
            for assertion in &self.assertions {
                match assertion.kind.as_str() {
                    "event_seen" => {
                        let event = assertion.event.as_deref().ok_or_else(|| {
                            ScenarioError::Invalid("event_seen assertion has no event".to_string())
                        })?;
                        if lotus_trace::EventCategory::from_id(event).is_none() {
                            return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                                "event_seen assertion names an unknown event: {event}"
                            )));
                        }
                    }
                    "no_worker_crash" | "frame_count" => {}
                    other => {
                        return Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(format!(
                            "unknown assertion type: {other}"
                        )))
                    }
                }
            }
    
            Ok(())
        }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        fn example_path() -> std::path::PathBuf {
            std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
                .join("../../specs/scenario-example.yaml")
                .to_path_buf()
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn example_scenario_loads_and_validates() {
            let scenario = Scenario::load(example_path()).expect("example scenario must load");
            assert_eq!(scenario.version, 1);
            assert_eq!(scenario.profile.worker_flavor, WorkerFlavor::Integration);
            assert!(scenario.validate().is_ok());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn unbounded_scenarios_are_rejected() {
            let mut scenario = Scenario::load(example_path()).unwrap();
            scenario.stop.max_frames = MAX_SCENARIO_FRAMES + 1;
            assert!(matches!(
                scenario.validate(),
                Err(ScenarioError::Invalid(_))
            ));
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn unknown_assertion_is_rejected() {
            let mut scenario = Scenario::load(example_path()).unwrap();
            scenario.assertions.push(Assertion {
                kind: "expect_magic".to_string(),
                event: None,
                count_at_least: None,
                minimum: None,
            });
            assert!(scenario.validate().is_err());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn unknown_event_name_is_rejected() {
            let mut scenario = Scenario::load(example_path()).unwrap();
            scenario.assertions.push(Assertion {
                kind: "event_seen".to_string(),
                event: Some("gpu.not_a_real_event".to_string()),
                count_at_least: Some(1),
                minimum: None,
            });
            assert!(scenario.validate().is_err());
        }
    }
    //! Lotus desktop application.
    //!
    //! This is the smallest possible GPUI shell: one window with an instance
    //! list and a placeholder for the two 3DS screens. The worker, the debugger
    //! views and the trace viewer are wired in later; the point of this spike is
    //! to prove that the pinned GPUI revision builds and opens a window on the
    //! host platform.
    
    use gpui::{
        div, prelude::*, px, rgb, size, App, Bounds, Context, Render, Window, WindowBounds,
        WindowOptions,
    };
    use gpui_platform::application;
    use lotus_desktop::{LotusUiState, SessionSummary};
    
    /// Root view of the Lotus window.
    struct LotusWindow {
        state: LotusUiState,
    }
    
    impl Render for LotusWindow {
        fn render(&mut self, _window: &mut Window, _cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
            let header = div()
                .flex()
                .items_center()
                .justify_between()
                .w_full()
                .h(px(40.0))
                .px_4()
                .border_b_1()
                .border_color(rgb(0x3a3a3a))
                .child("Lotus")
                .child(format!("worker protocol {}", self.state.protocol_version));

    fn instance_row(session: &SessionSummary) -> impl IntoElement {

            .px_2()
            .py_1()

    }

            .expect("cannot open the Lotus window");

    void System::ProcessPendingWork() {
        // Processes work that needs to run on the emulation thread. This function is called from
        // two places, the RunLoop slice and during the frame limiter wait period.
        // To wake up the frame limiter so that it processes more work, other threads must call
        // NotifyPendingWork.
    
    #ifdef ENABLE_GDBSTUB
        if (GDBStub::IsServerEnabled()) {

    #endif
    
    #ifdef ENABLE_SCRIPTING
        if (rpc_server) {
            rpc_server->ProcessCoreRequests();
        }
    #endif
    }
    
    void System::ProcessPendingWorkUntil(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point deadline) {
        do {
            ProcessPendingWork();
        } while (pending_work_event.WaitUntil(deadline));
    }
    
    void System::NotifyPendingWork() {
        pending_work_event.Set();
    }
    
    bool System::SendSignal(System::Signal signal, u32 param) {
        std::scoped_lock lock{signal_mutex};
        if (current_signal != signal && current_signal != Signal::None) {
            LOG_ERROR(Core, "Unable to {} as {} is ongoing", signal, current_signal);
            return false;
        }
        current_signal = signal;
        signal_param = param;

        [[nodiscard]] ResultStatus RunLoop(bool tight_loop = true);
    
        /**
         * Runs one pass of all the work that must happen on the emulation thread outside of guest
         * execution (such as GDB or scripting requests). Called by RunLoop between slices and from
         * the frame limiter.
         */
        void ProcessPendingWork();
    
        /**
         * Runs ProcessPendingWork until the deadline, sleeping in between until either the deadline
         * passes or NotifyPendingWork is called. The frame limiter calls this instead of sleeping.
         * Must be called from the emulation thread.
         */
        void ProcessPendingWorkUntil(std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point deadline);
    
        /**
         * Wakes up the emulation thread if it is waiting in ProcessPendingWorkUntil, so that newly
         * queued work is processed right away. This function is thread safe.
         */
        void NotifyPendingWork();
    
        /**

        [[nodiscard]] ResultStatus SingleStep();

    namespace SwRenderer {
    
    RendererSoftware::RendererSoftware(Core::System& system, Pica::PicaCore& pica_,
                                       Frontend::EmuWindow& window)
        : VideoCore::RendererBase{system, window, nullptr}, memory{system.Memory()}, pica{pica_},
          rasterizer{memory, pica} {}
    
    RendererSoftware::~RendererSoftware() = default;
    
    void RendererSoftware::SwapBuffers() {
        system.perf_stats->StartSwap();
        PrepareRenderTarget();
        system.perf_stats->EndSwap();
        EndFrame();
    }
    
    void RendererSoftware::PrepareRenderTarget() {
        const auto& regs_lcd = pica.regs_lcd;
        for (u32 i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
            const u32 fb_id = i == 2 ? 1 : 0;
    
            const auto color_fill = fb_id == 0 ? regs_lcd.color_fill_top : regs_lcd.color_fill_bottom;
            LoadFBToScreenInfo(i, color_fill);
        }
    }
    
    void RendererSoftware::LoadFBToScreenInfo(int i, const Pica::ColorFill& color_fill) {
        const u32 fb_id = i == 2 ? 1 : 0;
        const auto& framebuffer = pica.regs.framebuffer_config[fb_id];
        auto& info = screen_infos[i];
    
        const PAddr framebuffer_addr =
            framebuffer.active_fb == 0 ? framebuffer.address_left1 : framebuffer.address_left2;
        const s32 bpp = Pica::BytesPerPixel(framebuffer.color_format);
        const u8* framebuffer_data = memory.GetPhysicalPointer(framebuffer_addr);
    
        const s32 pixel_stride = framebuffer.stride / bpp;
        info.height = framebuffer.height;
        info.width = pixel_stride;
        info.pixels.resize(info.width * info.height * 4);
    
        for (u32 y = 0; y < info.height; y++) {
            for (u32 x = 0; x < info.width; x++) {
                const u8* pixel = framebuffer_data + (y * pixel_stride + pixel_stride - x) * bpp;
                Common::Vec4 color = [&] {
                    if (color_fill.is_enabled) {
                        return Common::Vec4<u8>(color_fill.color_r, color_fill.color_g,
                                                color_fill.color_b, 255);
                    }
    
                    switch (framebuffer.color_format) {
                    case Pica::PixelFormat::RGBA8:
                        return Common::Color::DecodeRGBA8(pixel);
                    case Pica::PixelFormat::RGB8:
                        return Common::Color::DecodeRGB8(pixel);
                    case Pica::PixelFormat::RGB565:
                        return Common::Color::DecodeRGB565(pixel);
                    case Pica::PixelFormat::RGB5A1:
                        return Common::Color::DecodeRGB5A1(pixel);
                    case Pica::PixelFormat::RGBA4:
                        return Common::Color::DecodeRGBA4(pixel);
                    }
                    UNREACHABLE();
                }();
                const u32 output_offset = (x * info.height + y) * 4;
                u8* dest = info.pixels.data() + output_offset;
                std::memcpy(dest, color.AsArray(), sizeof(color));
            }
        }
    }

    std::vector<SinkDetails> ListSinks() {
        return {sink_details.begin(), sink_details.end()};

    const SinkDetails& GetSinkDetails(SinkType sink_type) {
        auto iter = std::find_if(
            sink_details.begin(), sink_details.end(),
            [sink_type](const auto& sink_detail) { return sink_detail.type == sink_type; });
    
        if (sink_type == SinkType::Auto || iter == sink_details.end()) {
            if (sink_type != SinkType::Auto) {
                LOG_ERROR(Audio, "AudioCore::GetSinkDetails given invalid sink_type {}", sink_type);
            }
            // Auto-select.
            // sink_details is ordered in terms of desirability, with the best choice at the front.
            iter = sink_details.begin();
        }
    
        return *iter;
    }

    namespace Input {
    
    /// An abstract class template for an input device (a button, an analog input, etc.).
    template <typename StatusType>
    class InputDevice {
    public:
        virtual ~InputDevice() = default;
        virtual StatusType GetStatus() const {
            return {};
        }
    };
    
    /// An abstract class template for a factory that can create input devices.
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    class Factory {
    public:
        virtual ~Factory() = default;
        virtual std::unique_ptr<InputDeviceType> Create(const Common::ParamPackage&) = 0;
    };
    
    namespace Impl {
    
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    using FactoryListType = std::unordered_map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<Factory<InputDeviceType>>>;
    
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    struct FactoryList {
        static FactoryListType<InputDeviceType> list;
    };
    
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    FactoryListType<InputDeviceType> FactoryList<InputDeviceType>::list;
    
    } // namespace Impl
    
    /**
     * Registers an input device factory.
     * @tparam InputDeviceType the type of input devices the factory can create
     * @param name the name of the factory. Will be used to match the "engine" parameter when creating
     *     a device
     * @param factory the factory object to register
     */
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    void RegisterFactory(const std::string& name, std::shared_ptr<Factory<InputDeviceType>> factory) {
        auto pair = std::make_pair(name, std::move(factory));
        if (!Impl::FactoryList<InputDeviceType>::list.insert(std::move(pair)).second) {
            LOG_ERROR(Input, "Factory {} already registered", name);
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Unregisters an input device factory.
     * @tparam InputDeviceType the type of input devices the factory can create
     * @param name the name of the factory to unregister
     */
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    void UnregisterFactory(const std::string& name) {
        if (Impl::FactoryList<InputDeviceType>::list.erase(name) == 0) {
            LOG_ERROR(Input, "Factory {} not registered", name);
        }
    }
    
    /**
     * Create an input device from given parameters.
     * @tparam InputDeviceType the type of input devices to create
     * @param params a serialized ParamPackage string contains all parameters for creating the device
     */
    template <typename InputDeviceType>
    std::unique_ptr<InputDeviceType> CreateDevice(const std::string& params) {
        const Common::ParamPackage package(params);
        const std::string engine = package.Get("engine", "null");
        const auto& factory_list = Impl::FactoryList<InputDeviceType>::list;
        const auto pair = factory_list.find(engine);
        if (pair == factory_list.end()) {
            if (engine != "null") {
                LOG_ERROR(Input, "Unknown engine name: {}", engine);
            }
            return std::make_unique<InputDeviceType>();
        }
        return pair->second->Create(package);
    }
    
    /**
     * A button device is an input device that returns bool as status.
     * true for pressed; false for released.
     */
    using ButtonDevice = InputDevice<bool>;
    
    /**
     * An analog device is an input device that returns a tuple of x and y coordinates as status. The
     * coordinates are within the unit circle. x+ is defined as right direction, and y+ is defined as up
     * direction
     */
    using AnalogDevice = InputDevice<std::tuple<float, float>>;
    
    /**
     * A motion device is an input device that returns a tuple of accelerometer state vector and
     * gyroscope state vector.
     *
     * For both vectors:
     *   x+ is the same direction as LEFT on D-pad.
     *   y+ is normal to the touch screen, pointing outward.
     *   z+ is the same direction as UP on D-pad.
     *
     * For accelerometer state vector
     *   Units: g (gravitational acceleration)
     *
     * For gyroscope state vector:
     *   Orientation is determined by right-hand rule.
     *   Units: deg/sec
     */
    using MotionDevice = InputDevice<std::tuple<Common::Vec3<float>, Common::Vec3<float>>>;
    
    /**
     * A touch device is an input device that returns a tuple of two floats and a bool. The floats are
     * x and y coordinates in the range 0.0 - 1.0, and the bool indicates whether it is pressed.
     */
    using TouchDevice = InputDevice<std::tuple<float, float, bool>>;
    
    } // namespace Input

    enum class AcceptedInput {
        Anything,            /// All inputs are accepted.
        NotEmpty,            /// Empty inputs are not accepted.
        NotEmptyAndNotBlank, /// Empty or blank inputs (consisting solely of whitespace) are not
                             /// accepted.
        NotBlank,    /// Blank inputs (consisting solely of whitespace) are not accepted, but empty
                     /// inputs are.
        FixedLength, /// The input must have a fixed length (specified by maxTextLength in
                     /// swkbdInit).
    };
    
    enum class ButtonConfig {
        Single, /// Ok button
        Dual,   /// Cancel | Ok buttons
        Triple, /// Cancel | I Forgot | Ok buttons
        None,   /// No button (returned by swkbdInputText in special cases)
    };
    
    enum class KeyboardType {
        Normal,
        QWERTY,
        NumPad,
        Western,
    };
    
    /// Default English button text mappings. Frontends may need to copy this to internationalize it.
    constexpr char SWKBD_BUTTON_OKAY[] = "Ok";
    constexpr char SWKBD_BUTTON_CANCEL[] = "Cancel";
    constexpr char SWKBD_BUTTON_FORGOT[] = "I Forgot";
    
    /// Configuration thats relevent to frontend implementation of applets. Anything missing that we
    /// later learn is needed can be added here and filled in by the backend HLE applet
    struct KeyboardConfig {
        KeyboardType type = KeyboardType::Normal;
        ButtonConfig button_config;
        AcceptedInput accept_mode; /// What kinds of input are accepted (blank/empty/fixed width)
        bool multiline_mode;       /// True if the keyboard accepts multiple lines of input
        u16 max_text_length;       /// Maximum number of letters allowed if its a text input
        u16 max_digits;            /// Maximum number of numbers allowed if its a number input
        std::string hint_text;     /// Displayed in the field as a hint before
        std::vector<std::string> button_text; /// Contains the button text that the caller provides
        struct Filters {
            bool prevent_digit;     /// Limit maximum digit count to max_digits
            bool prevent_at;        /// Disallow the use of the @ sign.
            bool prevent_percent;   /// Disallow the use of the % sign.
            bool prevent_backslash; /// Disallow the use of the \ sign.
            bool prevent_profanity; /// Disallow profanity using Nintendo's profanity filter.
            bool enable_callback;   /// Use a callback in order to check the input.
        };
        Filters filters;
    };
    
    struct KeyboardData {
        std::string text;
        u8 button{};
    };
    
    enum class ValidationError {
        None,
        // Button Selection
        ButtonOutOfRange,
        // Configured Filters
        MaxDigitsExceeded,
        AtSignNotAllowed,
        PercentNotAllowed,
        BackslashNotAllowed,
        ProfanityNotAllowed,
        CallbackFailed,
        // Allowed Input Type
        FixedLengthRequired,
        MaxLengthExceeded,
        BlankInputNotAllowed,
        EmptyInputNotAllowed,
    };
    
    class SoftwareKeyboard {
    public:
        virtual ~SoftwareKeyboard() = default;
    
        /**
         * Executes the software keyboard, configured with the given parameters.
         */
        virtual void Execute(const KeyboardConfig& config_) {
            config = config_;
        }
    
        /**
         * Whether the result data is ready to be received.
         */
        bool DataReady() const;
    
        /**
         * Receives the current result data stored in the applet, and clears the ready state.
         */
        const KeyboardData& ReceiveData();
    
        /**
         * Shows an error text returned by the callback.
         */
        virtual void ShowError(const std::string& error) = 0;
    
        /**
         * Validates if the provided string breaks any of the filter rules. This is meant to be called
         * whenever the user input changes to check to see if the new input is valid. Frontends can
         * decide if they want to check the input continuously or once before submission
         */
        ValidationError ValidateFilters(const std::string& input) const;
    
        /**
         * Validates the the provided string doesn't break any extra rules like "input must not be
         * empty". This will be called by Finalize but can be called earlier if the frontend needs
         */
        ValidationError ValidateInput(const std::string& input) const;
    
        /**
         * Verifies that the selected button is valid. This should be used as the last check before
         * closing.
         */
        ValidationError ValidateButton(u8 button) const;
    
        /**
         * Runs all validation phases. If successful, stores the data so that the HLE applet in core can
         * send this to the calling application
         */
        ValidationError Finalize(const std::string& text, u8 button);
    
    protected:
        KeyboardConfig config;
        KeyboardData data;
    
        bool data_ready = false;
    };
    
    class DefaultKeyboard final : public SoftwareKeyboard {
    public:
        explicit DefaultKeyboard(Core::System& system_);
        void Execute(const KeyboardConfig& config) override;
        void ShowError(const std::string& error) override;
    
    private:
        Core::System& system;
    };

    <p><a id="toplevel-functions"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="qualify-calls-to-top-level-functions-with-a-module-name">Qualify calls to top-level functions with a module name</h3>
    
    <p>To use top-level functions defined in other modules or crates, import their
    module and call them with <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">modulename::functionname()</code>. For example:</p>
    
    <div class="goodcode"></div>
    
    <div class="language-rust highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">use</span> <span class="nn">std</span><span class="p">::</span><span class="n">mem</span><span class="p">;</span>
    
    <span class="k">let</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nn">mem</span><span class="p">::</span><span class="nf">transmute</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">y</span><span class="p">);</span>
    </code></pre></div></div>
    
    <div class="badcode"></div>
    
    <div class="language-rust highlighter-rouge"><div class="highlight"><pre class="highlight"><code><span class="k">use</span> <span class="nn">std</span><span class="p">::</span><span class="nn">mem</span><span class="p">::</span><span class="n">transmute</span><span class="p">;</span>
    
    <span class="k">let</span> <span class="n">x</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">transmute</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">y</span><span class="p">);</span>
    </code></pre></div></div>
    
    <p>Exceptions:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>When importing functions with sufficiently disambiguated names, e.g.,
    functions from C++ (where it is typical to call top-level (free) functions
    directly).</li>
      <li>
        <p>In Chromium, when importing functions from
    <a href="#small-crates">small, single-purpose first-party crates</a>.</p>
      </li>
      <li>When the module name itself is prone to collisions. For example, when the
    module name is a C++ namespace name, and multiple crates define the same
    submodules.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>Many Rust codebases consistently keep a style such that unqualified lowercase
    names are assumed local, so <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">foo()</code> can be assumed to be from the same module.
    This rule largely exists to avoid reviewer disagreements, the benefit is mostly
    consistency and a minor edge on reading code without xrefs.</p>
    
    <p><a id="type-names"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="type-names-should-be-imported-and-used-unqualified">Type names should be imported and used unqualified</h3>
    
    <p>By default, types and traits should be referenced in code without using their
    module path, e.g., code should use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Regex</code>, not <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">regex::Regex</code>, with a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">use
    regex::Regex</code> at the top of the file or potentially in the relevant function.</p>
    
    <p>Exceptions:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>In cases where there are ambiguities, it is acceptable to directly reference
    types with common names like <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">io::Error</code>. It is also acceptable to rename
    (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">use std::io::Error as IoError</code>).</li>
      <li>In cases where you have a large “group” of types, e.g. the
    <a href="https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_hir/hir/index.html"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hir module in rustc</code></a>
    which contains a large number of HIR types.</li>
      <li>In macros and generated code; where requiring a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">use</code> is counterproductive.</li>
      <li>In code with lots of dependencies, where importing everything would lead to
    a very large import block with little benefit.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>This rule largely exists to avoid reviewer disagreements.</p>
    
    <p><a id="import-macro"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="use-the-appropriate-import-mechanism-chrome">Use the appropriate import mechanism <span class="chrome">[chrome]</span></h3>
    
    <ul>
      <li><span class="chrome">Chrome</span> Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">chromium::import!()</code>.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p><a id="code-formatting"></a></p>
    
    <h2 id="code-formatting-and-aesthetics">Code formatting and aesthetics</h2>
    
    <p><a id="formatting-other"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="use-the-appropriate-formatting-tool">Use the appropriate formatting tool</h3>
    
    <p>Use the appropriate formatting tool (e.g., <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">git cl format</code> in Chromium).</p>
    
    <p>Configuration (for style guide authors)</p>
    
    <p>A codebase may choose to not apply the following <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">rustfmt</code> options if they care
    about building on stable and the option is unavailable on their stable Rust:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>
        <p>Maximum of 100 columns per line:
    <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/rustfmt/?version=v1.6.0&amp;search=#max_width"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">max_width = 100</code></a></p>
      </li>
      <li>
        <p>Usage of lowercase alphabets in hex literals (<code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0xab123cdef</code> as opposed to
    <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">0xAB123CDEF</code>):
    <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/rustfmt/?version=v1.6.0&amp;search=#hex_literal_case"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">hex_literal_case = Lower</code></a></p>
      </li>
      <li>
        <p>Macro matcher formatting:
    <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/rustfmt/?version=v1.6.0&amp;search=#format_macro_matchers"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">format_macro_matchers = true</code></a></p>
      </li>
      <li>
        <p>Usage of escapes for invisible characters in literals. E.g., if you wish to
    have text containing a Zero-Width joiner, use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">\u{200D}</code>.</p>
      </li>
    </ul>
    
    <p><a id="formatting-optout"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="opting-out-of-automatic-formatting">Opting out of automatic formatting</h3>
    
    <p>You may opt out of automatic formatting using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">#[rustfmt::skip]</code>, but only in
    the following situations:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li><strong>Manual alignment</strong> – If you have a situation-specific reason to have a
    snippet of code line up in a particular way (e.g., multiple similar lines of
    code that you want to remain aligned for readability, or a
    matrix-constructing function).</li>
      <li><strong>Generated code</strong> (ideally, use a genrule instead).</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>Important: Formatting should not be skipped for personal style choices.</p>
    
    <p><a id="ownership-borrowing"></a></p>
    
    <h2 id="ownership-and-borrowing">Ownership and borrowing</h2>
    
    <p><a id="avoid-rc-arc"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="avoid-rc-and-arc">Avoid <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rc</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arc</code></h3>
    
    <p>Prefer unique ownership and borrowing over <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rc</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arc</code> for managing memory.</p>
    
    <p>Exception:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rc</code> and <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arc</code> when the alternative ownership and borrowing structure
    would be unreasonably complex to write, understand, or maintain. This is a
    judgment call to be discussed during code review.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>Generally, Rust allows representing object graphs without using shared ownership
    smart pointers. These pointers add runtime overhead and their own unique
    complexity. Engineers coming from other languages might tend to use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rc</code> and
    <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arc</code> too quickly.</p>
    
    <p><a id="prefer-borrows"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="prefer-borrows-over-deep-copies">Prefer borrows over deep copies</h3>
    
    <p>Use <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.clone()</code> when you genuinely need a deep copy of an object.</p>
    
    <p>Avoid using <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.clone()</code> as a substitute for borrowing. Design code that works
    naturally with Rust’s ownership and borrowing rules. However, if the borrowing
    relationships become excessively complex, <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">.clone()</code> can be a pragmatic choice.</p>
    
    <p>Consider the performance needs of the code while choosing between cloning and
    borrowing.</p>
    
    <p>Note: This advice does not apply to cloning <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Rc</code> or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Arc</code> pointers. Cloning
    reference-counted pointers does not create a deep copy, and is an expected way
    to use them.</p>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>Deep copies can be expensive to make due to memory allocation and data copying.</p>
    
    <p><a id="inputs-and-outputs"></a></p>
    
    <h2 id="function-inputs-and-outputs">Function inputs and outputs</h2>
    
    <p><a id="flexible-references"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="accept-flexible-references-for-immutable-data">Accept flexible references for immutable data</h3>
    
    <p>When functions accept borrowed, immutable data, use a reference type that
    affords the most flexibility. Pass references to the data itself instead of
    references to smart pointers, containers, or wrappers.</p>
    
    <!-- mdformat off(keep table rows on single lines for Kramdown compatibility in the public style guide) -->
    
    <table>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>Use</th>
          <th>Instead of</th>
          <th>Why?</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;T</code></td>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;Box&lt;T&gt;</code></td>
          <td>Borrow the data inside the box</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;[T]</code></td>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;Vec&lt;T&gt;</code></td>
          <td>Accept any slice instead of specific containers</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;str</code></td>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;String</code></td>
          <td>Accept a string slice instead of references to owned strings</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Option&lt;&amp;T&gt;</code></td>
          <td><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;Option&lt;T&gt;</code></td>
          <td>Borrow the data inside the Option</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
    
    <!-- mdformat on -->
    
    <p>Exceptions:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>When expecting non-linear character data such as Rope/Cord.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>For context, see Clippy lints
    <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#borrowed_box"><code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">borrowed_box</code></a>
    and
    <a href="https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#ptr_arg">ptr_arg</a>.</p>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>Accepting reference types that don’t mention specific smart pointers,
    containers, or wrappers makes functions more versatile and performant: callers
    can pass data held in a variety of ways without copying it first.</p>
    
    <p><a id="return-iterators"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="iterators-vs-owned-collections-in-return-types">Iterators vs. owned collections in return types</h3>
    
    <p>Prefer returning iterators (either concrete types or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">impl Iterator</code>) where
    possible over returning <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Vec&lt;T&gt;</code>.</p>
    
    <p>Note: In application code, returning a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">Vec&lt;T&gt;</code> is fine if it simplifies the
    code and if flexibility and performance advantages of iterators are not clearly
    needed.</p>
    
    <p>Exceptions:</p>
    
    <ul>
      <li>Most callers will need to construct an owned vector.</li>
      <li>The function’s implementation naturally constructs a vector.</li>
      <li>The returned value will likely need to be randomly indexed.</li>
      <li>The algorithm works better as a <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">for</code> loop and the forced allocation doesn’t
    matter too much.</li>
      <li>The function’s intended purpose is creating a new owned collection.</li>
      <li>The function is returning a pre-existing vector.</li>
    </ul>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
    
    <p>Highly reusable library code generally should strive to provide more flexible
    and performant APIs. Returning an iterator allows callers to choose how to
    consume the data: collect it into a vector, process it in a loop, or chain
    further iterator adapters. Some of these options allow users to avoid
    unnecessary allocations.</p>
    
    <p>In application code, the usage patterns for a function are often easier to
    predict. If it is clear that performance is not a concern, or that data would be
    collected into a vector anyway, returning a vector makes for a simpler API.</p>
    
    <p><a id="accept-iterators"></a></p>
    
    <h3 id="iterators-vs-slices-in-function-parameters">Iterators vs. slices in function parameters</h3>
    
    <p>Highly reusable library code should accept iterators or <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">impl IntoIterator</code> if
    it only needs to iterate over the input.</p>
    
    <p>Note: In application code, accepting a slice <code class="language-plaintext highlighter-rouge">&amp;[T]</code> is fine if it simplifies the
    code and if flexibility and performance advantages of iterators are not clearly
    needed.</p>
    
    <p>Rationale</p>
