    ValidationError SoftwareKeyboard::Finalize(const std::string& text, u8 button) {
        // Skip check when OK is not pressed
        if (button == static_cast<u8>(config.button_config)) {
            ValidationError error;
            if ((error = ValidateInput(text)) != ValidationError::None) {
                return error;
            }
            if ((error = ValidateButton(button)) != ValidationError::None) {
                return error;
            }
        }
        data = {text, button};
        data_ready = true;
        return ValidationError::None;
    }
    
    bool SoftwareKeyboard::DataReady() const {
        return data_ready;
    }
    
    const KeyboardData& SoftwareKeyboard::ReceiveData() {
        data_ready = false;
        return data;
    }
    
    DefaultKeyboard::DefaultKeyboard(Core::System& system_) : system(system_) {}
    
    void DefaultKeyboard::Execute(const Frontend::KeyboardConfig& config_) {
        SoftwareKeyboard::Execute(config_);
    
        auto cfg = Service::CFG::GetModule(system);
        std::string username = Common::UTF16ToUTF8(cfg->GetUsername());
        switch (this->config.button_config) {
        case ButtonConfig::None:
        case ButtonConfig::Single:
            Finalize(username, 0);
            break;
        case ButtonConfig::Dual:
            Finalize(username, 1);
            break;
        case ButtonConfig::Triple:
            Finalize(username, 2);
            break;
        default:
            UNREACHABLE();
        }
    }
    
    void DefaultKeyboard::ShowError(const std::string& error) {
        LOG_ERROR(Applet_SWKBD, "Default keyboard text is unaccepted! error: {}", error);
    }

    std::vector<Mii::MiiData> LoadMiis() {
        std::vector<Mii::MiiData> miis;
    
        std::string nand_directory{FileUtil::GetUserPath(FileUtil::UserPath::NANDDir)};
        FileSys::ArchiveFactory_ExtSaveData extdata_archive_factory(nand_directory,
                                                                    FileSys::ExtSaveDataType::Shared);
    
        auto archive_result = extdata_archive_factory.Open(Service::PTM::ptm_shared_extdata_id, 0);
        if (archive_result.Succeeded()) {
            auto archive = std::move(archive_result).Unwrap();
    
            FileSys::Path file_path = "/CFL_DB.dat";
            FileSys::Mode mode{};
            mode.read_flag.Assign(1);
    
            auto file_result = archive->OpenFile(file_path, mode);
            if (file_result.Succeeded()) {
                auto file = std::move(file_result).Unwrap();
    
                u32 saved_miis_offset = 0x8;
                // The Mii Maker has a 100 Mii limit on the 3ds
                for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
                    Mii::MiiData mii;
                    std::array<u8, sizeof(mii)> mii_raw;
                    file->Read(saved_miis_offset, sizeof(mii), mii_raw.data());
                    std::memcpy(&mii, mii_raw.data(), sizeof(mii));
                    if (mii.mii_id != 0u) {
                        miis.push_back(mii);
                    }
                    saved_miis_offset += sizeof(mii);
                }
            }
        }
    
        return miis;
    }
    
    void DefaultMiiSelector::Setup(const Frontend::MiiSelectorConfig& config) {
        MiiSelector::Setup(config);
        Finalize(0, HLE::Applets::MiiSelector::GetStandardMiiResult().selected_mii_data);
    }

    /// Generic ARM11 CPU interface
    class ARM_Interface : NonCopyable {
    public:
        explicit ARM_Interface(u32 id, std::shared_ptr<Core::Timing::Timer> timer)
            : timer(timer), id(id) {};
        virtual ~ARM_Interface() {}
    
        struct ThreadContext {
            u32 GetStackPointer() const {
                return cpu_registers[13];
            }
            void SetStackPointer(u32 value) {
                cpu_registers[13] = value;
            }
    
            u32 GetLinkRegister() const {
                return cpu_registers[14];
            }
            void SetLinkRegister(u32 value) {
                cpu_registers[14] = value;
            }
    
            u32 GetProgramCounter() const {
                return cpu_registers[15];
            }
            void SetProgramCounter(u32 value) {
                cpu_registers[15] = value;
            }
    
            std::array<u32, 16> cpu_registers{};
            u32 cpsr{};
            std::array<u32, 64> fpu_registers{};
            u32 fpscr{};
            u32 fpexc{};
    
        private:
            friend class boost::serialization::access;
    
            template <class Archive>
            void serialize(Archive& ar, const unsigned int file_version) {
                ar & cpu_registers;
                ar & fpu_registers;
                ar & cpsr;
                ar & fpscr;
                ar & fpexc;
            }
        };
    
        /// Runs the CPU until an event happens
        virtual void Run() = 0;
    
        /// Step CPU by one instruction
        virtual void Step() = 0;
    
        /// Clear all instruction cache
        virtual void ClearInstructionCache() = 0;
    
        /**
         * Invalidate the code cache at a range of addresses.
         * @param start_address The starting address of the range to invalidate.
         * @param length The length (in bytes) of the range to invalidate.
         */
        virtual void InvalidateCacheRange(u32 start_address, std::size_t length) = 0;
    
        /// Clears the exclusive monitor's state.
        virtual void ClearExclusiveState() = 0;
    
        /// Notify CPU emulation that page tables have changed
        virtual void SetPageTable(const std::shared_ptr<Memory::PageTable>& page_table) = 0;
    
        /**
         * Set the Program Counter to an address
         * @param addr Address to set PC to
         */
        virtual void SetPC(u32 addr) = 0;
    
        /**
         * Get the current Program Counter
         * @return Returns current PC
         */
        virtual u32 GetPC() const = 0;
    
        /**
         * Get an ARM register
         * @param index Register index (0-15)
         * @return Returns the value in the register
         */

    //! Mock worker for process/transport acceptance; this never emulates a console.
    use std::io;
    
    use lotus_protocol::control::{self, Method, Reply, Request, Status};
    
    fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
        let mode = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_default();
        let mut input = io::stdin().lock();
        let mut output = io::stdout().lock();
        let mut identity: Option<String> = None;
        loop {
            let request: Request = control::read(&mut input)?;
            if mode == "crash" || (mode == "crash_status" && request.method == Method::Status) {
                std::process::exit(23);
            }
            if mode == "hang" {
                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(60));
                continue;
            }
            let status = if !lotus_protocol::is_compatible(request.version_major, request.version_minor)
            {
                Status::Unsupported
            } else if request.session.len() != 32
                || !request.session.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_hexdigit())
                || request.request_id == 0
            {
                Status::InvalidArgument
            } else if identity.as_ref().is_some_and(|id| id != &request.session) {
                Status::PermissionDenied
            } else if request.method != Method::Hello && identity.is_none() {
                Status::NotReady
            } else if request.epoch != 1 {
                Status::StaleEpoch
            } else {
                if request.method == Method::Hello {
                    identity = Some(request.session.clone());
                }
                Status::Ok
            };
            let stopped = status == Status::Ok && request.method == Method::Stop;
            let reply = Reply {
                version_major: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MAJOR,
                version_minor: lotus_protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION_MINOR,
                request_id: request.request_id,
                session: request.session,
                epoch: if mode == "stale" { 0 } else { 1 },
                status,
                state: if stopped { "stopped" } else { "idle" }.into(),
                backend: "mock".into(),
            };
            control::write(&mut output, &reply)?;
            if stopped {
                return Ok(());
            }
        }
    }
    //! Worker process lifecycle and session isolation.
    //!
    //! One emulator instance is one OS process running the native Azahar worker.
    //! The session manager owns those processes, their private storage roots and
    //! their state. It never links against `Core::System` and it never lets a
    //! worker failure take down the application or a sibling instance.
    
    pub mod storage;
    pub mod worker;
    
    pub use storage::StorageLayout;
    pub use worker::{WorkerFlavor, WorkerLaunchError, WorkerProcess, WorkerSpec};
    
    use lotus_protocol::capabilities::ConsoleModel;
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::collections::BTreeMap;
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    
    /// Identifier of a single emulator instance.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
    pub struct SessionId(pub u128);
    
    impl std::fmt::Display for SessionId {
        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
            write!(f, "session-{:032x}", self.0)
        }
    }
    
    /// Lifecycle state of a session.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum SessionState {
        /// Created, worker not started yet.
        Created,
        /// Worker running, content not loaded.
        Idle,
        /// Content loaded, emulation running.
        Running,
        /// Content loaded, emulation paused at a safe point.
        Paused,
        /// Worker exited normally.
        Stopped,
        /// Worker exited unexpectedly.
        Crashed,
    }
    
    impl SessionState {
        /// Whether the session can still issue emulation commands.
        pub fn is_active(&self) -> bool {
            matches!(
                self,
                SessionState::Idle | SessionState::Running | SessionState::Paused
            )
        }
    }
    
    /// Configuration of a session.
    ///
    /// Every field that affects execution must be recorded in a run manifest so
    /// that a result can be reproduced from a known configuration.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct SessionConfig {

        pub model: ConsoleModel,

    //! Native worker process handling.
    //!
    //! The worker is a separate OS process running a modified Azahar core. This
    //! module owns starting it, handing it its private storage and stopping it
    //! without leaving orphans behind.
    
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::process::{Child, Command, Stdio};
    use thiserror::Error;
    
    /// Azahar branch flavour a worker was built from.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    pub enum WorkerFlavor {
        /// `integration` branch: upstream minimal worker hooks.
        Integration,
        /// `experimental` branch: tracing, debugger and accuracy work.
        Experimental,
    }
    
    impl WorkerFlavor {
        /// Branch name on the Azahar fork.
        pub fn branch(&self) -> &'static str {
            match self {
                WorkerFlavor::Integration => "integration",
                WorkerFlavor::Experimental => "experimental",
            }
        }
    }
    
    /// Errors raised while launching or supervising a worker.
    #[derive(Debug, Error)]
    pub enum WorkerLaunchError {
        /// The worker executable was not found.
        #[error("worker executable not found: {0}")]
        NotFound(PathBuf),
        /// The worker could not be started.
        #[error("failed to launch worker: {0}")]
        Launch(#[source] std::io::Error),
    }
    
    /// How a worker process should be started.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    pub struct WorkerSpec {
        /// Path of the worker executable.
        pub executable: PathBuf,
        /// Private storage root handed to the worker.
        pub storage_root: PathBuf,
        /// Additional command line arguments.
        pub args: Vec<String>,
        /// Environment variables added to the worker environment.
        pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
    }
    
    impl WorkerSpec {
        /// A worker that runs against `storage_root`.
        pub fn new(executable: impl Into<PathBuf>, storage_root: impl Into<PathBuf>) -> Self {
            Self {
                executable: executable.into(),
                storage_root: storage_root.into(),
                args: Vec::new(),
                env: Vec::new(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Add a command line argument.
        pub fn arg(mut self, arg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            self.args.push(arg.into());
            self
        }
    
        /// Add an environment variable.
        pub fn env(mut self, key: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
            self.env.push((key.into(), value.into()));
            self
        }
    }
    
    /// A running worker process.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct WorkerProcess {
        child: Child,
        executable: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl WorkerProcess {
        /// Start a worker.
        pub fn spawn(spec: &WorkerSpec) -> Result<Self, WorkerLaunchError> {
            if !spec.executable.is_file() {
                return Err(WorkerLaunchError::NotFound(spec.executable.clone()));
            }
    
            let mut command = Command::new(&spec.executable);
            command
                .args(&spec.args)
                .envs(spec.env.iter().cloned())
                .env("LOTUS_STORAGE_ROOT", &spec.storage_root)
                .stdin(Stdio::null())
                .stdout(Stdio::null())
                .stderr(Stdio::null());
    
            #[cfg(windows)]
            {
                use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
                // Do not let the worker pop a console window on Windows.
                command.creation_flags(0x0800_0000);
            }
    
            let child = command.spawn().map_err(WorkerLaunchError::Launch)?;
            Ok(Self {
                child,
                executable: spec.executable.clone(),
            })
        }
    
        /// Process id of the worker.
        pub fn pid(&self) -> u32 {
            self.child.id()
        }
    
        /// Path of the worker executable.
        pub fn executable(&self) -> &Path {
            &self.executable
        }

    //! Real child-process acceptance, not an in-memory transport simulation.
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_session::controlled_worker::ControlledWorker;
    use lotus_session::{SessionState, WorkerSpec};
    
    fn spec(mode: &str) -> WorkerSpec {
        let id = lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid::generate();
        WorkerSpec::new(
            env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_lotus-mock-worker"),
            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lotus-control-{id}")),
        )
        .arg(mode)
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn handshake_query_clean_shutdown_and_second_launch() {
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let spec = spec("");
            let mut worker = ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
                .await
                .expect("mock handshake");
            let reply = worker.status().await.expect("status over pipes");
            assert_eq!(reply.backend, "mock");
            worker.stop().await.expect("graceful exit");
            assert_eq!(worker.state(), SessionState::Stopped);
            assert!(
                worker.status().await.is_err(),
                "stopped connection cannot be reused"
            );
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("remove test storage");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn failed_handshakes_are_reaped_and_logs_retained() {
        for mode in ["crash", "stale", "hang"] {
            let spec = spec(mode);
            assert!(
                ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_millis(500))
                    .await
                    .is_err(),
                "{mode} must fail"
            );
            assert!(spec.storage_root.join("worker.stderr.log").is_file());
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("child has released its files");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn four_private_connections_survive_a_sibling_failure() {
        let mut workers = Vec::new();
        let mut specs = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..4 {
            let spec = spec("");
            workers.push(
                ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
                    .await
                    .expect("spawn isolated child"),
            );
            specs.push(spec);
        }
        assert!(
            ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec("crash"), Duration::from_secs(3))
                .await
                .is_err()
        );
        for (mut worker, spec) in workers.into_iter().zip(specs) {
            worker.status().await.expect("sibling remains responsive");
            worker.stop().await.expect("sibling exits");
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("remove test storage");
        }
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn running_child_crash_transitions_to_crashed() {
        let spec = spec("crash_status");
        let mut worker = ControlledWorker::spawn(&spec, Duration::from_secs(3))
            .await
            .expect("handshake before crash");
        assert!(worker.status().await.is_err());
        assert_eq!(worker.state(), SessionState::Crashed);
        assert!(
            worker.status().await.is_err(),
            "failed commands cannot be retried"
        );
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(spec.storage_root).expect("reaped child releases log");
    }

    #pragma once
    #include <filesystem>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <json.hpp>
    #include "core/core.h"
    #include "video_core/gpu.h"
    #include "video_core/renderer_software/renderer_software.h"
    
    namespace CtrWorker {
    // Three reusable slots. A consumer copies before asking for another capture.
    // No UI acknowledgement or retained guest pointers can stall the core.
    inline nlohmann::json Capture(Core::System& system, const std::filesystem::path& root,
                                  u64 epoch, u64 sequence) {
        const auto& renderer = static_cast<const SwRenderer::RendererSoftware&>(system.GPU().Renderer());
        nlohmann::json frames = nlohmann::json::array();
        std::filesystem::create_directories(root / "frames");
        for (const auto& [name, id, width] : {
                 std::tuple{"top", VideoCore::ScreenId::TopLeft, 400u},
                 std::tuple{"bottom", VideoCore::ScreenId::Bottom, 320u}}) {
            const auto& source = renderer.Screen(id);
            if (source.width != 240 || source.height != width || source.pixels.size() != width * 240 * 4)
                throw std::runtime_error("unsupported framebuffer layout");
            auto pixels = source.pixels;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < pixels.size(); i += 4) std::swap(pixels[i], pixels[i + 2]);
            const auto relative = "frames/" + std::string{name} + "-" + std::to_string(sequence % 3) + ".bgra";
            std::ofstream file{root / relative, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc};
            file.exceptions(std::ios::failbit | std::ios::badbit);
            // Windows/Linux supported hosts are little endian; wire header uses explicit shifts.
            file.write("LTRF", 4);
            const auto write_le = [&file](u64 value, unsigned bytes) {
                for (unsigned i = 0; i < bytes; ++i) file.put(static_cast<char>(value >> (i * 8)));
            };
            write_le(1, 4); write_le(epoch, 8); write_le(sequence, 8);
            write_le(width, 4); write_le(240, 4);
            file.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(pixels.data()), pixels.size());
            file.close();
            frames.push_back({{"screen", name}, {"path", relative}, {"epoch", epoch},
                              {"sequence", sequence}, {"slot", sequence % 3}, {"width", width},
                              {"height", 240}, {"stride", width * 4}, {"format", "bgra8"},
                              {"orientation", "top_left_row_major"}, {"bytes", pixels.size()}});
        }
        return frames;
    }
    } // namespace CtrWorker

    // Bounded muted sink. DSP execution continues; no host audio device is opened.
    #pragma once
    #include <array>
    #include <mutex>
    #include "audio_core/sink.h"
    
    namespace AudioCore {
    struct WorkerAudioStats {
        u64 samples = 0;
        u64 dropped = 0;
        u64 hash = 14695981039346656037ull;
        size_t buffered = 0;
    };
    class WorkerSink final : public Sink {
    public:
        inline static std::mutex mutex;
        inline static std::array<s16, 32768> ring{};
        inline static WorkerAudioStats stats;
        unsigned GetNativeSampleRate() const override { return native_sample_rate; }
        void SetCallback(std::function<void(s16*, std::size_t)>) override {}
        bool ImmediateSubmission() override { return true; }
        void PushSamples(const void* data, std::size_t count) override {
            const auto* samples = static_cast<const s16*>(data);
            std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
            for (size_t i = 0; i < count * 2; ++i) {
                ring[(stats.samples * 2 + i) % ring.size()] = samples[i];
                const auto value = static_cast<u16>(samples[i]);
                stats.hash = (stats.hash ^ (value & 255)) * 1099511628211ull;
                stats.hash = (stats.hash ^ (value >> 8)) * 1099511628211ull;
            }
            stats.samples += count;
            const auto total = stats.buffered + count;
            stats.dropped += total > ring.size() / 2 ? total - ring.size() / 2 : 0;
            stats.buffered = std::min(total, ring.size() / 2);
        }
        static WorkerAudioStats Drain() {
            std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
            const auto snapshot = stats;
            stats.buffered = 0;
            return snapshot;
        }
        static void Reset() {
            std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
            stats = {};
        }
    };
    } // namespace AudioCore

    struct InputState {

        float y = 0;
        bool touch = false;
    };
    class Button final : public Input::ButtonDevice {
    public:
        Button(const InputState& state, unsigned index) : state(state), index(index) {}
        bool GetStatus() const override { return (state.buttons & (1u << index)) != 0; }
    private:
        const InputState& state;
        unsigned index;
    };
    class ButtonFactory final : public Input::Factory<Input::ButtonDevice> {
    public:
        explicit ButtonFactory(const InputState& state) : state(state) {}
        std::unique_ptr<Input::ButtonDevice> Create(const Common::ParamPackage& params) override {
            const auto index = params.Get("index", 0);
            if (index < 0 || index >= Settings::NativeButton::NumButtons)
                return std::make_unique<Input::ButtonDevice>();
            return std::make_unique<Button>(state, index);
        }
    private:
        const InputState& state;
    };
    class Touch final : public Input::TouchDevice {
    public:
        explicit Touch(const InputState& state) : state(state) {}
        std::tuple<float, float, bool> GetStatus() const override { return {state.x, state.y, state.touch}; }
    private:
        const InputState& state;
    };
    class TouchFactory final : public Input::Factory<Input::TouchDevice> {
    public:
        explicit TouchFactory(const InputState& state) : state(state) {}
        std::unique_ptr<Input::TouchDevice> Create(const Common::ParamPackage&) override {
            return std::make_unique<Touch>(state);
        }
    private:
        const InputState& state;
    };
    inline void RegisterInput(InputState& state) {
        Input::RegisterFactory<Input::ButtonDevice>("ctr", std::make_shared<ButtonFactory>(state));
        Input::RegisterFactory<Input::TouchDevice>("ctr", std::make_shared<TouchFactory>(state));
        auto& profile = Settings::values.current_input_profile;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < profile.buttons.size(); ++i)
            profile.buttons[i] = "engine:ctr,index:" + std::to_string(i);
        profile.touch_device = "engine:ctr";
    }
    } // namespace CtrWorker

    #pragma once
    #include <atomic>
    #include <chrono>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <thread>
    #include <json.hpp>
    #ifdef _WIN32
    #include <windows.h>
    #include <fcntl.h>
    #include <io.h>
    #else
    #include <poll.h>
    #include <unistd.h>
    #endif
    
    namespace CtrWorker {
    // Poll inherited stdin so stopping can join the reader without orphan threads.
    inline bool ReadExact(char* data, size_t size, const std::atomic_bool& stop) {
        while (size && !stop) {
    #ifdef _WIN32
            DWORD available = 0;
            const auto handle = GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE);
            if (!PeekNamedPipe(handle, nullptr, 0, nullptr, &available, nullptr)) return false;
            if (!available) { std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1)); continue; }
            DWORD received = 0;
            if (!ReadFile(handle, data, static_cast<DWORD>(std::min<size_t>(size, available)), &received, nullptr) || !received)
                return false;
    #else
            pollfd descriptor{STDIN_FILENO, POLLIN, 0};
            if (poll(&descriptor, 1, 10) <= 0) continue;
            const auto received = read(STDIN_FILENO, data, size);
            if (received <= 0) return false;
    #endif
            data += received;
            size -= received;
        }
        return size == 0;
    }
    inline bool Receive(nlohmann::json& request, const std::atomic_bool& stop) {
        unsigned char prefix[4];
        if (!ReadExact(reinterpret_cast<char*>(prefix), 4, stop)) return false;
        const u32 size = u32{prefix[0]} | (u32{prefix[1]} << 8) | (u32{prefix[2]} << 16) | (u32{prefix[3]} << 24);
        if (!size || size > 65536) return false;
        std::string payload(size, '\0');
        if (!ReadExact(payload.data(), size, stop)) return false;
        request = nlohmann::json::parse(payload, nullptr, false);
        return !request.is_discarded();
    }
    inline void Send(const nlohmann::json& reply) {
        const auto payload = reply.dump();
        if (payload.size() > 65536) throw std::runtime_error("reply exceeds control bound");
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) std::cout.put(static_cast<char>(payload.size() >> (i * 8)));
        std::cout.write(payload.data(), payload.size());
        std::cout.flush();
        if (!std::cout) throw std::runtime_error("control pipe disconnected");
    }
    } // namespace CtrWorker

    namespace CtrWorker {
    using Json = nlohmann::json;
    class Control {
    public:
        explicit Control(std::string root) : root(std::filesystem::absolute(root)) {}
        int Run() {
    #ifdef _WIN32
            _setmode(_fileno(stdout), _O_BINARY);
    #endif
            Initialize(system, root.string(), unsupported);
            RegisterInput(input);
            Settings::values.output_type = AudioCore::SinkType::Worker;
            Frontend::control_callback = [this] { Drain(true); };
            std::thread reader{[this] {
                while (!stopping) {
                    Json request;
                    if (!Receive(request, stopping)) break;
                    {
                        std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
                        if (queue.size() >= 16) break;
                        queue.push_back(std::move(request));
                    }
                    system.NotifyPendingWork();
                }
                disconnected = true;
                system.NotifyPendingWork();
            }};
            try {
                while (!stopping && !disconnected) {
                    Drain(false);
                    if (state == "running") {
                        const auto result = system.RunLoop();
                        if (result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success || unsupported ||
                            window.frames >= target || std::chrono::steady_clock::now() >= deadline) {
                            state = "paused";
                            last_error = unsupported ? "unsupported_applet" :
                                result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success ? "core_error" :
                                window.frames < target ? "host_deadline" : "";
                            if (pending_run) {
                                Reply(*pending_run, last_error.empty() ? "ok" : unsupported ? "unsupported" : "not_ready", Snapshot());
                                pending_run.reset();
                            }
                        }
                    } else {
                        system.ProcessPendingWorkUntil(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
                    }
                }
            } catch (const std::exception& error) {
                std::cerr << "worker_control_error: " << error.what() << '\n';
                exit_code = 1;
            }
            stopping = true;
            reader.join();
            Frontend::control_callback = {};
            if (system.IsPoweredOn()) system.Shutdown();
            Common::Log::Stop();
            return exit_code;
        }
    private:
        Json Snapshot() {
            const auto audio = AudioCore::WorkerSink::Drain();
            return {{"source", CTR_SOURCE_SHA}, {"frames", window.frames}, {"last_error", last_error},
                    {"input_owner", owner}, {"buttons", input.buttons}, {"touch_down", input.touch},
                    {"audio_samples", audio.samples}, {"audio_dropped", audio.dropped},
                    {"audio_hash_fnv1a64", audio.hash}, {"audio_buffered", audio.buffered}};
        }
        void Reply(const Json& request, const std::string& status, Json data = nullptr) {
            Send({{"version_major", 1}, {"version_minor", 0}, {"request_id", request.at("request_id")},
                  {"session", request.at("session")}, {"epoch", epoch}, {"status", status},
                  {"state", state}, {"backend", "azahar_native_software"}, {"data", std::move(data)}});
        }
        void Drain(bool nested) {
            // Never destroy/reinitialize a core while inside its RunLoop/frame limiter.
            for (unsigned count = 0; count < 16; ++count) {
                Json request;
                {
                    std::scoped_lock lock{mutex};
                    if (queue.empty()) return;
                    const auto method = queue.front().value("method", std::string{});
                    if (nested && method != "status" && method != "registers" && method != "read_memory") return;
                    request = std::move(queue.front()); queue.pop_front();
                }
                Handle(request);
                if (stopping) return;
            }
        }
        void Handle(const Json& request) {
            // Invalid envelopes end the connection: there may be no trustworthy reply identity.
            if (!request.is_object() || !request.contains("request_id") || !request["request_id"].is_number_unsigned() ||
                request["request_id"].get<u64>() == 0 || !request.contains("session") || !request["session"].is_string() ||
                !request.contains("epoch") || !request["epoch"].is_number_unsigned() || !request.contains("method") ||
                !request["method"].is_string() || !request.contains("version_major") || !request.contains("version_minor"))
                throw std::runtime_error("invalid request envelope");
            for (const auto& [key, value] : request.items())
                if (key != "version_major" && key != "version_minor" && key != "request_id" && key != "session" &&
                    key != "epoch" && key != "method" && key != "params") throw std::runtime_error("unknown envelope field");
            const auto id = request["session"].get<std::string>();
            if (id.size() != 32 || id.find_first_not_of("0123456789abcdefABCDEF") != std::string::npos)
                throw std::runtime_error("invalid session");
            if (request["version_major"] != 1 || request["version_minor"] != 0) { Reply(request, "unsupported"); return; }
            if (!session.empty() && session != id) { Reply(request, "permission_denied"); return; }
            if (request["epoch"] != epoch) { Reply(request, "stale_epoch"); return; }
            const auto method = request["method"].get<std::string>();
            if (method == "hello" && session.empty()) session = id;
            if (session.empty()) { Reply(request, "not_ready"); return; }
            try {
                const auto params = request.value("params", Json::object());
                if (method == "hello" || method == "status") { Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot()); return; }
                if (method == "stop") {
                    state = "stopped";
                    if (system.IsPoweredOn()) system.Shutdown();
                    Reply(request, "ok"); stopping = true; return;
                }
                if (method == "load" || method == "reset") {
                    if (state == "running") { Reply(request, "not_ready"); return; }
                    const auto path = method == "load" ? params.at("path").get<std::string>() : content;
                    if (path.empty() || !std::filesystem::is_regular_file(path) || std::filesystem::path(path).extension() != ".3dsx") {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); return;
                    }
                    if (system.IsPoweredOn()) system.Shutdown();
                    unsupported = false; input = {}; window.frames = 0; last_error.clear();
                    AudioCore::WorkerSink::Reset();
                    const auto result = system.Load(window, path);
                    if (result != Core::System::ResultStatus::Success) {
                        if (system.IsPoweredOn()) system.Shutdown();
                        state = "idle"; Reply(request, "not_ready", {{"load_result", static_cast<u32>(result)}}); return;
                    }
                    content = path; state = "paused";
                    if (method == "reset") ++epoch;
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot()); return;
                }
                if (!system.IsPoweredOn()) { Reply(request, "not_ready"); return; }
                if (method == "run" || method == "run_until") {
                    if (state != "paused" || pending_run) { Reply(request, "not_ready"); return; }
                    const auto frames = params.at("frames").get<u64>();
                    if (frames == 0 || frames > 600) { Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); return; }
                    target = window.frames + frames;
                    deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(20);
                    state = "running";
                    if (method == "run_until") pending_run = request;
                    else Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "pause") {
                    state = "paused";
                    if (pending_run) { Reply(*pending_run, "not_ready", {{"reason", "interrupted"}}); pending_run.reset(); }
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "capture") {
                    if (!window.frames) { Reply(request, "not_ready"); return; }
                    Reply(request, "ok", {{"frames", Capture(system, root, epoch, ++capture_sequence)}, {"frame", window.frames}});
                } else if (method == "input") {
                    const auto requested_owner = params.at("owner").get<std::string>();
                    if (requested_owner != "live" && requested_owner != "scenario") { Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); return; }
                    if (owner == "scenario" && requested_owner != owner) { Reply(request, "permission_denied"); return; }
                    const auto buttons = params.value("buttons", 0u);
                    const auto x = params.value("x", 0u), y = params.value("y", 0u);
                    if (buttons >= (1u << Settings::NativeButton::NumButtons) || x >= 320 || y >= 240) {
                        Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); return;
                    }
                    owner = requested_owner;
                    input = {buttons, x / 320.0f, y / 240.0f, params.value("touch", false)};
                    Reply(request, "ok", Snapshot());
                } else if (method == "registers") {
                    const auto core = params.at("core").get<u32>();
                    if (core >= system.GetNumCores()) { Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); return; }
                    Json registers = Json::array();
                    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i) registers.push_back(system.GetCore(core).GetReg(i));
                    Reply(request, "ok", {{"core", core}, {"registers", registers}, {"cpsr", system.GetCore(core).GetCPSR()}, {"safe_point", true}});
                } else if (method == "read_memory") {
                    const auto address = params.at("address").get<u64>(), length = params.at("length").get<u64>();
                    const auto process = system.Kernel().GetCurrentProcess();
                    if (!process || length == 0 || length > 4096 || address + length > 0x100000000ull || address > 0xffffffffull) {

                    system.Memory().ReadBlock(*process, static_cast<u32>(address), bytes.data(), length);
                    Reply(request, "ok", {{"address", address}, {"bytes", bytes}, {"safe_point", true}});
                } else Reply(request, "unsupported");
            } catch (const Json::exception&) { Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); }
              catch (const std::filesystem::filesystem_error&) { Reply(request, "invalid_argument"); }
              catch (const std::runtime_error& error) { Reply(request, "unsupported", {{"reason", error.what()}}); }
        }
        Core::System& system = Core::System::GetInstance();
        std::filesystem::path root;
        Window window;
        InputState input;
        std::string session, content, last_error, state = "idle", owner = "live";
        u64 epoch = 1, target = 0, capture_sequence = 0;
        bool unsupported = false;
        int exit_code = 0;
        std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point deadline;
        std::optional<Json> pending_run;
        std::mutex mutex;
        std::deque<Json> queue;
        std::atomic_bool stopping = false, disconnected = false;
    };

    # 13 — Build system, CI, milestones, release and risk management
    
    ## Build philosophy
    
    Two technologies, two lockfiles and independent test pipelines:
    
    - Rust workspace: locked Rust toolchain, Cargo dependencies, pinned GPUI Git revision; builds desktop, CLI, session manager, trace/MCP libraries.
    - Azahar native worker: CMake/C++ with upstream submodules, pinned Azahar branch SHA, compiler, CMake options and dependency versions; builds worker executable and C++ tests.
    
    No requirement to compile GPUI and Azahar into one binary. IPC compatibility is tested with separate build outputs. Do not let the Rust build dynamically fetch Azahar's moving `master` during CI.
    
    ## Local development on Windows first
    
    Suggested prerequisites: Git, CMake, Ninja, C++ compiler/toolchain matching Azahar's supported build paths, Rust/Cargo, Python for small scripts where useful, Windows SDK/Vulkan tools for GPU backend. Use official Azahar build instructions for actual compiler versions; don't assume Microsoft/MSYS2/MXE settings from a past release remain valid. The source currently uses CMake >=3.25 and has platform-specific conditionals. On macOS/Linux, follow GPUI's platform prerequisites and Azahar's native build requirements separately.
    
    Suggested commands after implementation (not executable in untouched upstream):
    
    ```powershell
    cargo build --locked -p ctr-cli -p ctr-desktop -p ctr-supervisor
    cmake -S vendor/azahar -B build/native-integration -G Ninja -DENABLE_QT=OFF -DENABLE_LIBRETRO=OFF -DENABLE_CTR_WORKER=ON -DENABLE_SOFTWARE_RENDERER=ON
    cmake --build build/native-integration --target ctr-worker --config RelWithDebInfo
    cargo test --locked --workspace
    ctr-cli doctor --worker build/native-integration/src/ctr_worker/ctr-worker.exe
    ```
    
    **Do not cargo-build or invoke the worker from a post-build script that downloads copyrighted Nintendo files.** User firmware and game assets are external; fixtures can use self-authored homebrew programs.
    
    ## Continuous integration jobs
    
    | Job | Trigger | Gate |
    |---|---|---|
    | `rust-check` | every Rust PR | format, clippy, unit tests, no semver drift |
    | `gpui-compile` | GPUI/desktop PR | Windows build and smoke; Linux/macOS where runners available |
    | `azahar-integration-build` | integration PR/upstream sync | worker+stock Azahar compile, C++ tests, minimal native run |
    | `azahar-experimental-build` | experimental PR | same worker protocol, instrumentation tests |
    | `protocol-contract` | schema or worker PR | version negotiation, invalid inputs, CLI/MCP parity |
    | `worker-smoke` | worker or session PR | .3dsx launch, input, audio, two screens, stop/restart |
    | `multi-instance` | storage/supervisor PR | 4 sessions and fs isolation under fault injection |
    | `golden-corpus` | core/GPU PR | fixed binaries, GPU outputs and stable checkpoints |
    | `performance-regression` | selected nightly | baseline/diagnostic builds, median and p95 host cost, A/B |
    | `upstream-watch` | scheduled | latest upstream SHA, diff hotspots and license changes |
    | `hardware-data` | manual physical run | validates fixture metadata, units, hashes and statistics |
    
    GitHub CI cannot validate real 3DS hardware unless a controlled physical runner is built and explicitly maintained. Don't label emulator-only CI as hardware verification.
    
    ## Release profiles
    
    - `fast-play`: Azahar-compatible settings, accelerated renderer, low overhead, minimal tracing.
    - `debug`: breakpoint state, safe-point RPC, L1 event rings and artifacts, reasonable performance.
    - `capture`: selective L2/L3 GPU/CPU events, may pause guest or incur major slowdown.
    - `research`: experimental models with explicit version/config and measured uncertainty, not enabled by default without tests.
    
    A release manifest must record product version, worker source revision/branch, protocol, GPUI revision, compiler, dependencies, defaults, known unsupported functions, and license notices. Experimental builds must be visually distinguishable from integrated baseline in GUI and trace metadata.
    
    ## Exit gates, not arbitrary calendar deadlines
    
    ### Milestone M0 — reproducible sources
    
    - Pinned Azahar revision, GPL/license inventory, stock build works, two worktrees configured.
    - Minimal native worker target compiles with Qt/Libretro disabled where supported.
    - No feature claim yet.
    
    ### M1 — core boots headless
    
    - Program load and basic execution; emitted status and complete shutdown.
    - Software top/bottom frames and event ordering validated against stock Azahar in one known homebrew fixture.
    - Failing input/unsupported applet emits typed error, not hang.
    
    ### M2 — Rust supervisor and CLI
    
    - Native control IPC handshake and session state; pause/resume/reset/runs; isolated storage.
    - At least 2 workers; acceptance target 4 concurrent independent instances.
    - Repeatable scenario with fixed stop condition and output hash.
    
    ### M3 — GPUI usability
    
    - Both screens, touch mapping, controller input, live status and logs.
    - Dynamic frame content under synthetic and real worker; UI survives worker crash.
    - No required Qt windows or Libretro dependencies.
    
    ### M4 — developer debugging
    
    - CPU registers and disassembly, safe-point memory reads, breakpoints; kernel thread/process snapshots; consistent error semantics.
    - MCP and CLI command equivalence; agent reproduces a known crash through scenario runner.
    
    ### M5 — GPU captures
    
    - PICA command list, draw-at-state, texture versions, frame ID, output raw image and diff.
    - Instrumentation A/B test and missing/dropped event reporting.
    - Three representative rendering regressions diagnosed with captures.
    
    ### M6 — first hardware verified accuracy gain
    
    - Physical old-3DS fixture corpus exists; at least one meaningful independent behavior correction with before/after vs stock Azahar; held-out evidence.
    - No broad claim of perfect accuracy; known failures cataloged.

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Verifies that every pinned dependency still points at the recorded revision.
    
    .DESCRIPTION
        Checks four things:
    
          1. The vendored Azahar checkout is at the pinned integration commit.
          2. The submodule pointer recorded in the index matches that commit.
          3. Cargo.lock resolves GPUI to the pinned upstream commit.
          4. The active Rust toolchain is the pinned channel.
    
        Exits with 1 when any check fails.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    
    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
    if (Get-Variable -Name PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false
    }
    Import-Module (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'Pins.psm1') -Force
    
    $root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
    $pinsPath = Join-Path $root 'config\pins.toml'
    
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pinsPath)) {
        Write-Error "missing $pinsPath"
        exit 1
    }
    
    $pins = Read-Pins -Path $pinsPath
    $failures = 0
    
    function Test-Pin {
        param(
            [string]$Name,
            [bool]$Ok,
            [string]$Detail
        )
    
        if ($Ok) {
            Write-Host ("PASS  {0}: {1}" -f $Name, $Detail) -ForegroundColor Green
        } else {
            Write-Host ("FAIL  {0}: {1}" -f $Name, $Detail) -ForegroundColor Red
            $script:failures++
        }
    }
    
    # 1. Vendored Azahar checkout.
    $azaharRoot = Join-Path $root $pins['azahar']['vendor_path']
    $expectedAzahar = $pins['azahar']['integration_commit']
    
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $azaharRoot '.git')) {
        $actualAzahar = (& git -C $azaharRoot rev-parse HEAD).Trim()
        Test-Pin -Name 'azahar checkout' -Ok ($actualAzahar -eq $expectedAzahar) `
            -Detail ("expected {0}, found {1}" -f $expectedAzahar, $actualAzahar)
    } else {
        Test-Pin -Name 'azahar checkout' -Ok $false -Detail "no checkout at $azaharRoot"
    }
    
    # 2. Submodule pointer in the index.
    $hasHead = $null -ne (& git -C $root rev-parse --verify HEAD 2>$null)
    if ($hasHead) {
        $pointer = (& git -C $root ls-tree HEAD $pins['azahar']['vendor_path'])
        if ($pointer -match '^160000 commit ([0-9a-f]{40})') {
            Test-Pin -Name 'azahar submodule pointer' -Ok ($Matches[1] -eq $expectedAzahar) `
                -Detail ("index records {0}" -f $Matches[1])
        } else {
            Test-Pin -Name 'azahar submodule pointer' -Ok $false -Detail 'no submodule pointer in the index'
        }
    } else {
        Test-Pin -Name 'azahar submodule pointer' -Ok $false -Detail 'the repository has no commit yet'
    }
    
    # 3. GPUI revision in Cargo.lock.
    $lockPath = Join-Path $root 'Cargo.lock'
    $expectedGpui = $pins['gpui']['rev']
    
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $lockPath) {
        $lock = Get-Content -LiteralPath $lockPath -Raw
        $gpuiLocked = $lock -match [regex]::Escape("rev=$expectedGpui")
        Test-Pin -Name 'gpui lock entry' -Ok $gpuiLocked `
            -Detail ("expected rev {0} in Cargo.lock" -f $expectedGpui)
    } else {
        Test-Pin -Name 'gpui lock entry' -Ok $false -Detail 'Cargo.lock is missing'
    }
    
    # 4. Rust toolchain.
    $expectedRust = $pins['rust']['channel']
    //! Native screen geometry shared by synthetic display and input tests.
    
    /// Displayed bottom-screen rectangle in logical host pixels.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
    pub struct TouchTransform {
        pub left: f32,
        pub top: f32,
        pub width: f32,
        pub height: f32,
    }
    
    impl TouchTransform {
        /// Invert the actual displayed rectangle. Letterbox and outside clicks miss.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn map_logical(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Option<(u16, u16)> {
            if ![self.left, self.top, self.width, self.height, x, y]
                .iter()
                .all(|v| v.is_finite())
                || self.width <= 0.0
                || self.height <= 0.0
            {
                return None;
            }
            let x = (x - self.left) / self.width;
            let y = (y - self.top) / self.height;
            if !(0.0..1.0).contains(&x) || !(0.0..1.0).contains(&y) {
                return None;
            }
            Some(((x * 320.0).floor() as u16, (y * 240.0).floor() as u16))
        }
    
        /// Convert physical pointer coordinates using the window's actual DPI scale.
        #[must_use]
        pub fn map_physical(&self, x: f32, y: f32, dpi: f32) -> Option<(u16, u16)> {
            if !dpi.is_finite() || dpi <= 0.0 {
                return None;
            }
            self.map_logical(x / dpi, y / dpi)
        }
    }
    
    /// Generate normalized native-resolution BGRA pixels, as required by GPUI.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn pattern(width: u32, session: u8, sequence: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity(width as usize * 240 * 4);
        for y in 0..240 {
            for x in 0..width {
                pixels.extend_from_slice(&[x as u8 ^ sequence, y as u8, session * 60, 255]);
            }
        }
        pixels
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        #[test]
        fn touch_corners_and_center_survive_zoom_and_dpi() {
            for zoom in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0] {
                let transform = TouchTransform {
                    left: 113.0,
                    top: 71.0,
                    width: 320.0 * zoom,
                    height: 240.0 * zoom,
                };
                for dpi in [1.25, 2.0] {
                    for (x, y) in [(0, 0), (319, 0), (0, 239), (319, 239), (160, 120)] {
                        let host_x = (transform.left + (f32::from(x) + 0.5) * zoom) * dpi;
                        let host_y = (transform.top + (f32::from(y) + 0.5) * zoom) * dpi;
                        assert_eq!(transform.map_physical(host_x, host_y, dpi), Some((x, y)));
                    }
                }
                assert_eq!(transform.map_logical(112.0, 71.0), None);
                assert_eq!(
                    transform.map_logical(transform.left + transform.width, 71.0),
                    None
                );
            }
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn invalid_transforms_never_create_guest_coordinates() {
            let transform = TouchTransform {
                left: 0.0,
                top: 0.0,
                width: 320.0,
                height: 240.0,
            };
            assert_eq!(transform.map_physical(1.0, 1.0, 0.0), None);

    //! Windows job ownership. Children start suspended until containment is installed.
    use std::io;
    use std::mem;
    use std::os::windows::io::{AsRawHandle, FromRawHandle, OwnedHandle};
    use std::ptr;
    
    use windows_sys::Win32::Foundation::{INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, TRUE};
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Diagnostics::ToolHelp::{
        self, THREADENTRY32, TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::JobObjects::{
        self, JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation, JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION,
        JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE,
    };
    use windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading::{
        self, PROCESS_SET_QUOTA, PROCESS_TERMINATE, THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME,
    };
    
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub(crate) struct ProcessJob {
        handle: OwnedHandle,
    }
    
    impl ProcessJob {
        pub(crate) fn attach_and_resume(pid: u32) -> io::Result<Self> {
            // SAFETY: Windows returns owned handles. Each successful handle is wrapped
            // immediately, and all pointers refer to correctly sized live structures.
            unsafe {
                let raw = JobObjects::CreateJobObjectW(ptr::null(), ptr::null());
                if raw.is_null() {
                    return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                }
                let job = Self { handle: OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(raw) };
                let mut limits: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION = mem::zeroed();
                limits.BasicLimitInformation.LimitFlags = JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE;
                if JobObjects::SetInformationJobObject(raw, JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation,
                    ptr::from_ref(&limits).cast(), mem::size_of_val(&limits) as u32) == 0 {
                    return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                }
                let process = Threading::OpenProcess(PROCESS_SET_QUOTA | PROCESS_TERMINATE, 0, pid);
                if process.is_null() { return Err(io::Error::last_os_error()); }
                let process = OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(process);
                if JobObjects::AssignProcessToJobObject(raw, process.as_raw_handle()) == 0 {
                    return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                }
                let snapshot = ToolHelp::CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
                if snapshot == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE { return Err(io::Error::last_os_error()); }
                let snapshot = OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(snapshot);
                let mut entry: THREADENTRY32 = mem::zeroed();
                entry.dwSize = mem::size_of_val(&entry) as u32;
                let mut found = ToolHelp::Thread32First(snapshot.as_raw_handle(), &mut entry);
                while found == TRUE {
                    if entry.th32OwnerProcessID == pid {
                        let thread = Threading::OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME, 0, entry.th32ThreadID);
                        if thread.is_null() { return Err(io::Error::last_os_error()); }
                        let thread = OwnedHandle::from_raw_handle(thread);
                        if Threading::ResumeThread(thread.as_raw_handle()) == u32::MAX {
                            return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
                        }
                        return Ok(job);
                    }
                    found = ToolHelp::Thread32Next(snapshot.as_raw_handle(), &mut entry);
                }
                Err(io::Error::other("suspended worker thread not found"))
            }
        }
    }
    
    impl Drop for ProcessJob {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            // SAFETY: this live owned handle refers to our job. Termination is limited
            // to its members; closing the handle also enforces kill-on-close on panic.
            unsafe { JobObjects::TerminateJobObject(self.handle.as_raw_handle(), 1); }
        }
    }

    //! The server speaks MCP over stdio. It is local only: no TCP listener is

        Ok(())

    # Independent 3DS emulator — engineering dossier and workspace
    
    **Status:** scaffolded workspace plus design dossier. No emulator yet. **Research checked:** 2026-11-15. **Primary target:** original 2011 3DS; New 3DS later. **Host:** Windows first, macOS/Linux next. **UI:** Rust + Zed GPUI. **Initial emulation:** modified **Azahar native core**, **not Libretro**. **Long-term aim:** measurable hardware accuracy beyond Azahar/Citra.
    
    ## Start here
    
    1. [01 — Product contract](docs/01-product-contract.md): identity, goals, non-goals, metrics.
    2. [02 — Overall architecture](docs/02-system-architecture.md): Rust/GPUI + native C++ worker and runtime boundaries.
    3. [03 — Two-branch Azahar strategy](docs/03-azahar-branches.md): upstream tracking, integration vs experimental, commands and merge policy.
    4. [04 — Native worker implementation](docs/04-azahar-native-worker.md): file-by-file intervention points, build and bring-up.
    5. [05 — GPUI desktop](docs/05-gpui-desktop.md): native UI, input and video, debugging views.
    6. [06 — Protocol and lifecycle](docs/06-ipc-and-session-contract.md): transport, safe points, artifacts, failure handling.
    7. [07 — CPU/kernel/memory debugging](docs/07-debugger-core.md): precise debugger semantics, breaking, stepping and symbols.
    8. [08 — GPU inspection](docs/08-gpu-and-trace.md): draw capture, shader state, resource lineage, synchronized observation.
    9. [09 — MCP and agent automation](docs/09-mcp-and-scenarios.md): small safe tool API, reproducible scenarios, example workflow.
    10. [10 — Multi-instance operations](docs/10-multi-instance-and-storage.md): worker isolation, cloning, inputs, storage and limits.
    11. [11 — Accuracy roadmap](docs/11-accuracy-research.md): independent CPU/GPU/memory models and experimental method.
    12. [12 — Hardware validation](docs/12-hardware-validation.md): test harness, benchmarks, ground truth and statistics.
    13. [13 — Build, CI, acceptance](docs/13-build-test-release.md): milestones, matrices, exit gates and risk register.
    14. [14 — Sources and evidence](docs/14-sources-and-evidence.md): annotated direct code links and assumptions.
    15. [15 — Implementer task sequence](docs/15-implementation-tickets.md): dependency-ordered PRs with acceptance criteria.
    16. [16 — Azahar patch blueprint](docs/16-azahar-patch-blueprint.md): source files, native hooks, branch-specific patch sequence.
    17. [17 — Scaffold, pins and build instructions](docs/17-scaffold-and-pins.md): what exists, what is pinned, how to build it.
    18. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): mandatory rules for implementer/agents.
    
    Additional artifacts: [`specs/`](specs/) contains *proposed* protocol and scenario shapes; [`templates/`](templates/) contains review/experiment record formats. Protocol names and proposed code are not claims about existing Azahar APIs.
    
    ## What exists today
    
    The repository is scaffolded and builds. There is no emulator in it yet.
    
    | Part | State |
    | --- | --- |
    | Rust workspace (`crates/`) | **verified compiled**: protocol, session, trace, debugger, runner, hardware, accuracy, MCP, CLI and the GPUI shell; 51 tests pass; `fmt` and `clippy` clean |
    | GPUI desktop shell | **verified compiled** and launched: opens a window; screens are placeholders |
    | MCP server | **verified compiled**: serves `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` over stdio |
    | `ctr-cli` | **verified compiled**: `version`, `pins`, `scenario validate` |
    | Native worker (`workers/azahar`) | **verified compiled**: a protocol stub that prints its handshake; no Azahar core linked |
    | Vendored Azahar | **source present** at the pinned commit with all of its submodules; the core itself is **not built** on this host |
    | `workers/native`, `tools/hardware-tests` | **not started** |
    
    Everything above is pinned; see [`config/pins.toml`](config/pins.toml) and [17 — Scaffold and pins](docs/17-scaffold-and-pins.md).
    
    ## Getting started
    
    ```powershell
    # Toolchain, vendored sources, dependencies, pin verification.
    scripts\bootstrap.ps1
    
    # Fast checks: build, tests, CLI, pins.
    scripts\smoke.ps1
    
    # The pinned revisions, from the command line.
    cargo run --quiet --bin ctr-cli -- pins
    ```
    
    ## Repository layout
    
    ```
    lotus/
    ├── crates/          # Rust: protocol, session, trace, debugger, runner, hardware,
    │                    #        accuracy, mcp, cli, desktop
    ├── workers/azahar/  # C++ worker: ABI header, entry point, CMake
    ├── workers/native/  # future Rust emulation backend (not started)
    ├── vendor/azahar/   # pinned Azahar checkout (git submodule)
    ├── tools/           # devkitPro 3DS ground truth programs (not started)
    ├── tests/           # smoke, integration, differential, fixtures, scenarios
    ├── scripts/         # bootstrap, pin verification, native build, smoke
    ├── config/pins.toml # pinned source revisions
    └── docs/            # the dossier
    ```
    
    ## Architectural decision in one paragraph
    
    The Rust application **owns the product**: GPUI, sessions, CLI, MCP, tests, artifacts and long-lived debugger interfaces. Each emulator instance is a **separate OS process** running a deliberately modified Azahar C++ core through a **native worker frontend**, preserving existing CPU/kernel/graphics/audio functionality. Azahar is tracked in a **single fork with two enduring branches**: `integration` (upstream-minimal native worker hooks) and `experimental` (deeper instrumentation, accuracy changes). The worker and UI use versioned IPC. Hardware accuracy is pursued using separately validated components and physical-3DS experiments, never by declaring host frame time to be hardware time.
    
    ## Guarantees this dossier does not make
    
    - No emulator has been built. The native worker is a protocol stub; the Rust side is a shell.
    - The Azahar core has **not** been compiled on this host. The pinned commit is recorded in `config/pins.toml` and checked by `scripts/verify-pins.ps1`; do not assume code paths stay stable.
    - GPUI is pre-1.0: the commit is pinned and the smallest UI shell is compiled before any detail of its image API is adopted.
    - A `Headless` window enum is **not** proof that GPU readback, audio and applet integration work end to end without added code.
    - Citra/Azahar accuracy is not equivalent to hardware timing accuracy.
    - GPL/subcomponent licenses need review before distributing a combined application; no Nintendo firmware or keys are included.
    
    ## Non-negotiable project tests
    
    A test counts only when it is reproducible with fixed input, a known source/build hash, isolated storage and a bounded stop condition. Keep stock Azahar as an independent behavior baseline, and a physical Old 3DS as the authority for hardware claims. A trace must label **guest behavior**, **host performance**, and **estimated hardware timing** separately.
    
    ## Project naming
    
    Working name: **CTR emulator** (placeholder; rename the repository/project before publication). All examples use `ctr`/`ctr-worker` as placeholders. Do not build a protocol dependency on the name.

    //! Shared native operations used by desktop, CLI and MCP.
    use std::fs;
    use std::io;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::time::Duration;
    
    use lotus_protocol::control::{Method, Reply, Status};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    use serde_json::Value;
    
    use crate::controlled_worker::ControlledWorker;
    use crate::WorkerSpec;
    
    /// A file-ring lease. Reading checks identity before exposing owned pixel bytes.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
    pub struct FrameLease {
        pub screen: String,
        pub path: String,
        pub epoch: u64,
        pub sequence: u64,
        pub slot: u64,
        pub width: u32,
        pub height: u32,
        pub stride: u32,
        pub format: String,
        pub orientation: String,
        pub bytes: usize,
    }
    
    /// Native pixels copied out of a ring slot; independent of subsequent captures.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct Frame {
        pub lease: FrameLease,
        pub bgra: Vec<u8>,
    }
    
    /// Input is a complete state, so disconnect/release can always send zero.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct InputState {
        pub buttons: u32,
        pub x: u16,
        pub y: u16,
        pub touch: bool,
    }
    
    /// Owns one private native worker. Each command completes at an emulation safe point.
    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct NativeSession {
        worker: ControlledWorker,
        root: PathBuf,
    }
    
    impl NativeSession {
        pub async fn spawn(executable: &Path, root: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {
            let mut worker = ControlledWorker::spawn(&WorkerSpec::new(executable, root), Duration::from_secs(30)).await?;
            let reply = worker.status().await?;
            if reply.backend != "azahar_native_software" {
                worker.stop().await?;
                return Err(io::Error::other("worker lacks native software capability"));
            }
            Ok(Self { worker, root: root.to_path_buf() })
        }
    
        pub async fn load(&mut self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Load, serde_json::json!({"path": path.canonicalize()?})).await
        }
    
        /// Advance 1–600 presented frames, with a native 20s and supervisor 30s deadline.
        pub async fn advance(&mut self, frames: u16) -> io::Result<Value> {
            if frames == 0 || frames > 600 { return Err(io::Error::other("frame batch must be in 1..=600")); }
            self.operation(Method::RunUntil, serde_json::json!({"frames": frames})).await
        }
    
        pub async fn run(&mut self) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Run, serde_json::json!({"frames": 600})).await
        }
    
        pub async fn pause(&mut self) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Pause, Value::Null).await
        }
    
        pub async fn reset(&mut self) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Reset, Value::Null).await
        }
    
        pub async fn input(&mut self, state: InputState, owner: &str) -> io::Result<Value> {
            let mut params = serde_json::to_value(state).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            params["owner"] = owner.into();
            self.operation(Method::Input, params).await
        }
    
        pub async fn status(&mut self) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Status, Value::Null).await
        }
    
        pub async fn registers(&mut self, core: u32) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::Registers, serde_json::json!({"core": core})).await
        }
    
        pub async fn memory(&mut self, address: u32, length: u16) -> io::Result<Value> {
            self.operation(Method::ReadMemory, serde_json::json!({"address": address, "length": length})).await
        }
    
        pub async fn capture(&mut self) -> io::Result<Vec<Frame>> {
            let data = self.operation(Method::Capture, Value::Null).await?;
            let leases: Vec<FrameLease> = serde_json::from_value(data["frames"].clone()).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
            if leases.len() != 2 { return Err(io::Error::other("capture must contain exactly two native screens")); }
            leases.into_iter().map(|lease| {
                let bgra = read_frame(&self.root, &lease)?;
                Ok(Frame { lease, bgra })
            }).collect()
        }
    
        pub async fn stop(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> { self.worker.stop().await }
    
        /// Explicit failure injection and emergency termination, limited to this job.
        pub async fn abort(&mut self) { self.worker.abort().await; }
    
        #[must_use]
        pub fn root(&self) -> &Path { &self.root }
    
        async fn operation(&mut self, method: Method, params: Value) -> io::Result<Value> {
            let Reply { status, data, .. } = self.worker.command(method, params).await?;
            if status != Status::Ok { return Err(io::Error::other(format!("{method:?}: {status:?}: {data}"))); }
            Ok(data)
        }
    }
    
    /// A stale sequence, reset epoch, malformed header or path cannot expose pixels.
    pub fn read_frame(root: &Path, lease: &FrameLease) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        let expected_width = match lease.screen.as_str() { "top" => 400, "bottom" => 320, _ => 0 };
        let expected_path = format!("frames/{}-{}.bgra", lease.screen, lease.sequence % 3);
        if expected_width == 0 || lease.width != expected_width || lease.height != 240
            || lease.stride != lease.width * 4 || lease.bytes != (lease.stride * 240) as usize
            || lease.slot != lease.sequence % 3 || lease.path != expected_path
            || lease.format != "bgra8" || lease.orientation != "top_left_row_major" {
            return Err(io::Error::other("invalid frame lease"));
        }
        // Bound allocation before reading. The worker is serialized by mutable ownership.
        let path = root.join(expected_path);
        if fs::metadata(&path)?.len() != lease.bytes as u64 + 32 { return Err(io::Error::other("invalid frame size")); }
        let data = fs::read(path)?;
        let mut expected = Vec::with_capacity(32);
        expected.extend_from_slice(b"LTRF");
        expected.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&lease.epoch.to_le_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&lease.sequence.to_le_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&lease.width.to_le_bytes());
        expected.extend_from_slice(&lease.height.to_le_bytes());
        if data.len() != lease.bytes + 32 || data[..32] != expected { return Err(io::Error::other("stale or malformed frame slot")); }
        Ok(data[32..].to_vec())
    }

    //! Opt-in native acceptance. Assets remain outside Git; no network or ROM download.
    use std::path::PathBuf;
    
    use lotus_protocol::envelope::SessionUuid;
    use lotus_session::native_session::{InputState, NativeSession};
    
    fn config() -> (PathBuf, PathBuf, PathBuf) {
        let executable = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("LOTUS_NATIVE_WORKER").expect("set LOTUS_NATIVE_WORKER"));
        let fixture = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("LOTUS_FIXTURE").expect("set LOTUS_FIXTURE"));
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lotus-native-{}", SessionUuid::generate()));
        (executable, fixture, root)
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    #[ignore = "requires explicitly supplied native executable and homebrew fixture"]
    async fn native_lifecycle_frames_input_and_safe_reads() {
        let (executable, fixture, root) = config();
        let mut session = NativeSession::spawn(&executable, &root).await.expect("native handshake");
        assert!(NativeSession::spawn(&executable, &root).await.is_err(), "exclusive root lock");
        session.load(&fixture).await.expect("load homebrew");
        session.input(InputState { buttons: 1, ..InputState::default() }, "scenario").await.expect("exclusive input");
        assert!(session.input(InputState::default(), "live").await.is_err());
        session.input(InputState::default(), "scenario").await.expect("release buttons");
        let status = session.advance(60).await.expect("bounded run");
        assert_eq!(status["frames"], 60);
        let frames = session.capture().await.expect("native screens");
        assert_eq!(frames[0].bgra.len(), 400 * 240 * 4);
        assert_eq!(frames[1].bgra.len(), 320 * 240 * 4);
        let lease = frames[0].lease.clone();
        for _ in 0..3 { session.capture().await.expect("replace ring slots"); }
        assert!(session.read_lease(&lease).is_err(), "slot sequence invalidates lease");
        session.run().await.expect("start asynchronous run");
        for _ in 0..10 {
            let registers = session.registers(0).await.expect("safe read while running/limiting");
            assert_eq!(registers["safe_point"], true);
            let pc = registers["registers"][15].as_u64().expect("PC") as u32;
            session.memory(pc, 4).await.expect("mapped instruction memory");
            assert!(session.memory(pc, 4097).await.is_err(), "bounded read");
        }
        session.pause().await.expect("pause outside nested loop");
        let current = session.capture().await.expect("capture after pause");
        session.reset().await.expect("new epoch");
        assert!(session.read_lease(&current[0].lease).is_err(), "reset invalidates leases");
        session.advance(2).await.expect("run after reset");
        session.stop().await.expect("clean shutdown");
        let mut second = NativeSession::spawn(&executable, &root).await.expect("root lock released");
        second.load(&fixture).await.expect("second launch");
        second.advance(2).await.expect("second run");
        second.stop().await.expect("second shutdown");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).expect("all instance files released");
    }
    
    #[tokio::test]
    #[ignore = "requires explicitly supplied native executable and homebrew fixture"]
    async fn four_native_workers_survive_forced_sibling_failure() {
        let (executable, fixture, root) = config();
        let mut tasks = Vec::new();
        for index in 0..4 {
            let executable = executable.clone();
            let fixture = fixture.clone();
            let root = root.join(index.to_string());
            tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
                let mut session = NativeSession::spawn(&executable, &root).await.expect("isolated native child");
                session.load(&fixture).await.expect("same read-only content");
                session.advance(30).await.expect("parallel emulation");
                let frames = session.capture().await.expect("private frame artifacts");
                if index == 0 {
                    session.abort().await;
                    assert!(session.read_lease(&frames[0].lease).is_err());
                    assert!(session.status().await.is_err());
                } else {
                    session.advance(30).await.expect("surviving sibling");
                    session.stop().await.expect("clean sibling stop");
                }
                root
            }));
        }
        for task in tasks { let child_root = task.await.expect("worker test task"); assert!(child_root.join("worker.stderr.log").exists()); }
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(root).expect("job handles and locks released after crash");
    }

    //! Desktop application state.
    //!
    //! The GPUI layer owns presentation only. It never reaches into the native
    //! worker: it renders immutable snapshots that the session supervisor
    //! publishes.
    
    use lotus_session::{SessionId, SessionState};
    use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
    
    /// Summary of one emulator instance, as shown in the instance list.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct SessionSummary {
        /// Session identifier.
        pub id: String,
        /// Current lifecycle state.
        pub state: SessionState,
        /// Console model the session emulates.
        pub model: String,
        /// Render backend the session requested.
        pub renderer: String,
    }
    
    /// State of the desktop application.
    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    pub struct LotusUiState {
        /// Sessions known to the supervisor.
        pub sessions: Vec<SessionSummary>,
        /// Identifier of the selected session.
        pub selected: Option<String>,
        /// Worker protocol version the UI was built against.
        pub protocol_version: String,
    }
    
    impl LotusUiState {
        /// Create the initial state.
        pub fn new() -> Self {
            Self {
                sessions: Vec::new(),
                selected: None,
                protocol_version: lotus_protocol::protocol_id(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Summary of a session.
        pub fn summary(
            id: SessionId,
            state: SessionState,
            model: impl Into<String>,
            renderer: impl Into<String>,
        ) -> SessionSummary {
            SessionSummary {
                id: id.to_string(),
                state,
                model: model.into(),
                renderer: renderer.into(),
            }
        }
    
        /// Select a session by identifier.
        pub fn select(&mut self, id: &str) {
            if self.sessions.iter().any(|session| session.id == id) {
                self.selected = Some(id.to_string());
            }
        }
    
        /// Summary of the selected session.
        pub fn selected_session(&self) -> Option<&SessionSummary> {
            let selected = self.selected.as_ref()?;
            self.sessions.iter().find(|session| &session.id == selected)
        }
    }
    
    #[cfg(test)]
    mod tests {
        use super::*;
    
        #[test]
        fn selection_requires_a_known_session() {
            let mut state = LotusUiState::new();
            state.select("session-00000000000000000000000000000001");
            assert!(state.selected.is_none());
    
            state.sessions.push(SessionSummary {
                id: "session-1".to_string(),
                state: SessionState::Idle,
                model: "old3ds".to_string(),
                renderer: "software".to_string(),
            });
            state.select("session-1");
            assert_eq!(state.selected.as_deref(), Some("session-1"));
            assert!(state.selected_session().is_some());
        }
    
        #[test]
        fn protocol_version_is_reported() {
            assert_eq!(LotusUiState::new().protocol_version, "1.0");
        }
    }
